PatakonKeresztulVezetoUtKvizK5V3=Deep mulching - by covering the soil (which is spared from tilling) with a thick layer of organic material (leaf mold, hay, straw, bark), the soil stays cooler, evaporation is greatly reduced, and the vegetable garden remains productive even with less water.
PatakonKeresztulVezetoUtKvizK5V4=Building a rain garden—a sunken garden area that absorbs rainwater runoff from roofs or paved surfaces, directing it there instead of letting it flow into the sewer—creates a pleasant microclimate and increases biodiversity.
PatakonKeresztulVezetoUtKvizK5V5=Permeable paving – using fewer pavers and opting for grass-paving stones or gravel on garden paths instead of concrete, allowing water to seep directly into the soil.
PatakonKeresztulVezetoUtKvizK5V6=Composting – soil rich in humus can store much more water than depleted, hard soil.
PatakonKeresztulVezetoUtKvizK5V7=Reducing food waste – any food that is wasted, spoiled, or thrown away also represents a loss of water, because the raw materials and the water needed to produce the food—some of which is rainwater—are wasted.
PatakonKeresztulVezetoUtKvizK5V8=Using rainwater for toilet flushing and laundry—when used in the home, it reduces drinking water consumption; since it is soft water, less detergent is needed for laundry, it does not cause limescale buildup in the washing machine, and clothes remain soft and easy to iron.
PatakonKeresztulVezetoUtKvizK5V9=Drainage to the street or sewer system—rain falls exactly when and in the amount that the garden and nature need it, so you try to get rid of the rainwater.
PatakonKeresztulVezetoUtKvizK5M=Rainwater is best for plants. It is neutral or slightly alkaline, soft, and free of substances harmful to them, such as chlorine.\n\nCollecting and using rainwater is an environmentally friendly solution that supports the natural water cycle and reduces the use of drinking water.\n\nHousehold water management can extend beyond the garden: rainwater is not only excellent for watering, but can also be used for laundry, for example. Since it is soft water, there is no limescale buildup, which extends the lifespan of the washing machine and maintains its efficiency; additionally, the washed clothes are easy to iron even without fabric softener and remain pleasant and soft. n\nNumerous studies confirm that washing with rainwater is hygienically safe, as the presence of microorganisms in the washing machine stems almost exclusively from the dirt on the clothes and is virtually independent of the type of water used.\n\nIn Germany and many other countries, tap water is a protected food-grade resource, and flushing the toilet with drinking water is a huge waste—which is why another effective use for rainwater is flushing the toilet.\n\nIf we are reluctant to use valuable rainwater for this purpose, we can also recycle graywater generated in the household—water from showers that is directed into a collection tank can be used to flush the toilet, and the clean, cold water that initially flows from the shower can be collected in a bucket for other uses.

SzennyvizLevezetoCsoKvizK5=Toilet flushing is one of the biggest water wasters in households. Choose the solutions that help reduce the amount of water used by the toilet!
SzennyvizLevezetoCsoKvizK5V1=Dual-flush cisterns – buttons on modern tanks allow a choice between small and large flushes, reducing water use by up to half.
SzennyvizLevezetoCsoKvizK5V2=Flush-stop buttons – pressing the button a second time stops the flush at any moment, so only the necessary amount of water is used.
SzennyvizLevezetoCsoKvizK5V3=Weights and displacements in the tank – placing weights (such as a large stone or a plastic bottle filled with water) into older, large-capacity tanks displaces the water, meaning the tank refills with and uses less water.
SzennyvizLevezetoCsoKvizK5V4=Greywater recycling – slightly used water from the washing machine or bathroom sink is routed (through a filtration system) into the toilet tank and reused.
SzennyvizLevezetoCsoKvizK5V5=Integrated sink cisterns – a faucet built into the top of the toilet tank allows you to wash your hands with the refill water after flushing, and this soapy water is then used for the next flush.
SzennyvizLevezetoCsoKvizK5V6=Replacing a conventional tank with a much larger 20-liter tank – this large amount of water keeps the toilet clean much more efficiently. (INCORRECT)
SzennyvizLevezetoCsoKvizK5V7=Rainwater harvesting system – rainwater collected from the roof and mechanically filtered is brought into the house through a separate pipe system, which can supply the toilet and washing machine, and is also suitable for cleaning.
SzennyvizLevezetoCsoKvizK5V8=Composting (dry) toilet – requires no water at all; the waste covered with moisture-absorbing sawdust or coconut coir becomes odorless and turns into nutrient-rich compost over time.
SzennyvizLevezetoCsoKvizK5V9=Installing a sensor-based water flow control flushing system – automated sensor flushing optimizes the amount of water used.
SzennyvizLevezetoCsoKvizK5M=The correct answers demonstrate methods that can be used in households to either reduce the volume of water per flush (for example, with a bottle placed in the tank or a stop button) or entirely replace clean drinking water (with rainwater, greywater, or dry technology).\n\nHowever, it is important to repair faulty, leaking seals and valves immediately, as continuous, unnoticed water flow can result in a large amount of wasted water.\n\nThe incorrect answer—installing a large, 20-liter tank—achieves the exact opposite of water saving: with every single flush, it needlessly wastes multiple times the average amount of water.\n\nIf you travel by boat or airplane, you may see toilet flushing solutions that differ from households—such as vacuum toilets: instead of gravity and a lot of water, this technology uses air pressure (vacuum) for cleaning, so a small amount (<1 liter) of water per flush is sufficient.\n\nToilet flushing is one of the biggest wasters of drinking water: do everything you can to ensure that you turn as little drinking water as possible into blackwater (highly contaminated water) when using the toilet.

MuanyagHordoKvizK8=Which of the following individual commitments and everyday habits directly or indirectly help reduce the amount of plastic waste and microplastics entering rivers and oceans?
MuanyagHordoKvizK8V1=Replacing single-use plastics: Using water bottles, canvas tote bags, and reusable food containers instead of PET bottles, plastic bags, and plastic takeout containers.
MuanyagHordoKvizK8V2=Using microfibre filters or washing bags: Using specialized washing bags (e.g., Guppyfriend) or external filters attachable to washing machines (e.g., Planetcare) to capture microfibres shedding from synthetic clothing.
MuanyagHordoKvizK8V3=Checking cosmetic ingredients: Avoiding scrubs, shower gels, and toothpastes that contain microplastic beads (polyethylene, polypropylene).
MuanyagHordoKvizK8V4=Burning plastic at home with green garden waste: Burning accumulated household plastic packaging at home in the garden, as the high temperature of the fire converts polymers into biologically neutral ash and pure carbon (plastics consist of polymers and additives).
MuanyagHordoKvizK8V5=Washing clothes at lower temperatures and with liquid detergent: Shifting away from abrasive powder detergents and hot water, as these are proven to cause significantly more microfibre shedding from synthetic garments.
MuanyagHordoKvizK8V6=Avoiding littering in public spaces and discarding cigarette butts: Throwing trash (especially cigarette butts, which contain plastic filters) into closed bins so that wind and rain cannot wash them into storm drains and rivers.
MuanyagHordoKvizK8V7=Avoiding Fast Fashion: Buying fewer, more durable clothes made of natural materials (cotton, linen, wool) instead of poor-quality polyester and nylon garments.
MuanyagHordoKvizK8V8=Packaging-free shopping: Prioritizing zero-waste and bulk stores, as well as local markets, thereby radically reducing household plastic packaging waste.
MuanyagHordoKvizK8V9=Supporting sustainable marine fishing (MSC certification): Buying seafood certified to come from sustainable sources, which helps reduce the abandonment of "ghost nets" in the ocean.
MuanyagHordoKvizK8M=Nearly four-fifths of marine litter and microplastics originate from households, meaning our daily choices have a direct impact on ocean wildlife.\n\nEliminating single-use plastics and practicing conscious consumerism tackles waste directly at the source.\n\nUsing microfibre washing bags, choosing liquid detergents, washing at cooler temperatures, and avoiding cosmetics with microbeads prevent invisible microplastics from washing down the drain and into rivers.\n\nFurthermore, avoiding public littering is crucial because wind and rainwater sweep debris—such as plastic-based cigarette butts—from city streets into storm drains and the nearest waterways.\n\nThe incorrect option—burning plastic at home on an open flame or garden fire—is strictly prohibited and extremely polluting.\n\nThe temperature of a household fire is not high enough to safely break down polymers. Consequently, burning plastics releases highly toxic, carcinogenic gases (such as dioxins) into the air and groundwater.\n\nAdditionally, the remaining ash and semi-burnt microplastic particles leach into the soil with rain, ultimately ending up in rivers and oceans regardless.

MangroveUtKvizK1=What natural disaster can be triggered if an earthquake occurs on the ocean floor or near a coastline?

MangroveUtKvizK1M=Tsunamis are generated by shockwaves from earthquakes on the sea floor, which impulsively lift and shove the column of water above them.\n\nOn the open ocean, the leading wave of a tsunami travels fast but is almost imperceptible; as it nears the coast it slows down and can rise several stories above the water.\n\nThis mass of water has enormous kinetic energy and, once it reaches land, it floods and devastates the entire coastline.

MangroveUtKvizK2V1=no, because there is no way to artificially generate the shockwaves released when stress accumulated in the rocks of Earth’s crust is discharged

MangroveUtKvizK2M=Researchers have identified a new, human-induced type of earthquake near Canadian oil wells.\n\nThis new type has an artificial origin, and the technique often used for oil and gas extraction in the region—hydraulic fracturing—lies behind it.\n\nThe operation pumps large amounts of water into boreholes, causing rock-layer fractures—and small to larger earthquakes.\n\nThe process uses enormous quantities of water, which can jeopardize regional drinking-water supplies.\n\nWastewater is also a problem: it is often pumped underground using deep wells, the future consequences of which are unknown—just as we do not fully understand the interconnections of deep aquifer systems.

WCKvizK1=Are the following statements about the jet stream and the polar vortex true?
WCKvizK1V1=The jet stream is a fast-flowing, meandering air current that swirls high above Earth, whereas the polar vortex is essentially a cyclone—an area of low pressure and cold air over Earth’s North and South Poles.
WCKvizK1V2=In average winters, a lack of solar energy cools the polar regions, and winds encircle these cold areas. They form a stable polar vortex that, together with a correspondingly stable jet stream, prevents cold air from escaping.
WCKvizK1V3=Changes in jet-stream behavior due to warming may influence the polar vortex, but this cannot trigger a feedback chain that then alters the jet stream—otherwise, instead of seasonally appropriate weather we would experience extremes.
WCKvizK1M=Unusually heavy snowfall in Greece, surprisingly mild winters in Western Europe, and bone-chilling cold in the north.\n\nJet stream and polar vortex: if you haven’t heard of them yet, it’s worth remembering their names—these phenomena are behind the unusual winter weather.

WCKvizK2=Are the following statements about the AMOC (Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation) and the Gulf Stream true?
WCKvizK2V1=In the future, the warmer seawater carried by the current will be increasingly less able to participate in the Atlantic’s vertical water exchange. The circulation known as the AMOC—in which warm, less dense surface water flows to the Atlantic’s polar regions, cools and sinks, then returns southward at depth—is losing strength.
WCKvizK2V2=A major slowdown or shutdown of the AMOC—and the resulting impediment of the Gulf Stream—would mostly affect the oceans’ heat balance and nutrient transport, but would not impact weather on land, including in Northwestern Europe.
WCKvizK2V3=As Greenland’s ice melts, vast amounts of cold freshwater enter the surrounding seas, mix with the Gulf Stream’s northbound warm water, and impede its onward flow. The circulation slows and the atmosphere must take over more of the transport role. Because the specific heats of air and water differ by thousands of times, this strengthens meridional (north–south) airflow, causing weather extremes across much of Europe.
WCKvizK2M=Climate change is not merely about warming; it also brings increases in the number and intensity of extreme events.\n\nAcross most of Europe, weather is governed by two circulation patterns: the more predictable, less variable zonal flow, and the wilder north–south meridional flow.\n\nThe latter drives extremes and has become increasingly dominant as the balance has shifted in recent times.\n\nBehind this lies a transformation of the Gulf Stream’s upper branch—the North Atlantic Current—stretching from the Gulf of Mexico toward Greenland.

TeherautoKvizK8=Are the following statements about geoengineering (climate engineering) true?
TeherautoKvizK8V1=Because we have done relatively little to cut emissions in recent decades, some experts have concluded that we should find other methods to fight global warming. One such technique is geoengineering—the umbrella term for direct interventions in the planet’s energy balance—in other words, Earth’s functioning. It has two categories: SRM (solar radiation management) and CDR (carbon dioxide removal).
TeherautoKvizK8V2=Solar geoengineering (SRM) aims to reduce incoming solar energy—thus cooling Earth. There are three types: 1. thinning high-altitude cirrus clouds so more heat can escape from Earth’s atmosphere; 2. making low-lying marine clouds more reflective by seeding them with reflective particles (e.g., calcium carbonate—chalk dust); 3. filling the stratosphere with these same particles. This latter plan is similar to when the ash from an erupting volcano temporarily dims the Earth and thereby lowers the global average temperature.
TeherautoKvizK8V3=The tools of carbon dioxide removal and sequestration (CDR) are intended to increase the amount of heat energy that escapes from Earth into space. The essence is to remove the excess carbon dioxide from the atmosphere that causes the greenhouse effect. There are two types: 1. enhancing existing natural carbon-dioxide-absorbing processes (e.g., afforestation); 2. applying chemical processes to capture carbon dioxide directly from the air and store it in underground geological reservoirs (CCS—Carbon Capture and Storage).
TeherautoKvizK8M=Experts consider SRM methods in geoengineering to be uncertain, fear-driven, desperation-born solutions that carry many question marks and even more dangers.\n\nAccording to current scientific knowledge, geoengineering is nothing more than masking the original problem and the existing solutions that can be applied reliably and without risk (emissions reductions, adaptation, carbon removal and sequestration (CDR), etc.) with a highly risky, questionable, symptom-focused treatment.

TeherautoKvizK9=Scientists are urging, in an open letter, that plans related to climate engineering (SRM technologies aimed at reducing the impact of solar radiation—and thus warming) be abandoned. What arguments do they use to support this?
TeherautoKvizK9V1=an uncertain stopgap whose potential drawbacks far outweigh the benefits
TeherautoKvizK9V2=cannot be implemented in ways that are globally just, moral, socially and ethically acceptable
TeherautoKvizK9V3=the technologies would not affect different regions of the planet uniformly or always as intended
TeherautoKvizK9V4=would have unpredictable impacts on Earth’s climate, which could negatively affect food and water security
TeherautoKvizK9V5=experiments could, in the future, affect the lives of all inhabitants of the planet, reducing biodiversity
TeherautoKvizK9V6=optimism about climate engineering would sap momentum from efforts to reduce carbon-dioxide emissions
TeherautoKvizK9V7=merely symptomatic treatments that mask the real problem—the effects of carbon dioxide present in the atmosphere—instead of solving it
TeherautoKvizK9V8=would hinder the spread of clean energy, especially solar power
TeherautoKvizK9V9=Earth’s ecosystem is too complex for us to foresee all the consequences of such a far-reaching intervention
TeherautoKvizK9M=In recent years, the persistently high level of greenhouse-gas emissions and the already significant level of warming have turned many decision-makers’ and researchers’ attention toward technologies that try to influence warming by, for example, releasing reflective particles into the atmosphere.\n\nA joint statement by 60 scientists from universities and research institutes around the world stresses that the potential drawbacks of solutions aimed at reducing the impact of solar radiation far outweigh the benefits.\n\nTo prevent problems, they urge countries to agree internationally to end national funding for solar-radiation-modification (SRM) approaches, to halt harmful outdoor experiments, and to suspend the issuance of patents related to the technology.\n\nThe signatories emphasize that there is currently no global regulation in force—meaning any country, or even a billionaire with rockets, could begin experimenting with the technology.

KvizK03=According to analyses, one-third of prepared food ends up in the trash, which not only grows landfill mountains but also wastes the raw materials and energy needed to produce it. Which conscious steps allow you to reduce food waste most effectively in your daily life?
KvizK03V1=Conscious shopping planning: always writing a precise shopping list based on a weekly menu plan and never shopping while hungry.
KvizK03V2=Proper organization of the fridge and pantry: applying the FIFO principle (first in, first out), meaning placing older, expiring products at the front and new ones at the back.
KvizK03V3=Distinguishing between dates: recognizing the difference between "best before" (safe to consume after this date, at most its quality decreases) and "use by" (healthy until this date) expiration terms.
KvizK03V4=Proper food storage: storing food at the correct temperature and using airtight containers to preserve freshness.
KvizK03V5=Creative use of leftovers: transforming remaining food into new dishes (for example, using stale crescent rolls to make Bread and Butter Pudding, or leftover roast meat for toasted sandwiches).
KvizK03V6=Smart use of the freezer: freezing excess raw ingredients or prepared meals before they spoil.
KvizK03V7=Serving smaller portions: putting less food on your plate, because you can always go back for seconds, thus avoiding throwing away leftovers left on the plate.
KvizK03V8=Stockpiling discounted products: mostly buying promotional food close to its expiration date, often in bulk, regardless of whether you can consume it during the week, because it saves you more money.
KvizK03V9=Home composting: composting kitchen green waste, allowing valuable nutrients to return to the cycle.
KvizK03M=The fight against food waste begins in our own kitchens. According to statistics, households themselves are responsible for the majority of discarded food, meaning our individual decisions have tremendous power.\n\nExplanation of correct answers: conscious habits such as writing a shopping list, organizing the fridge (FIFO principle), or knowing expiration dates accurately prevent us from buying unnecessarily or letting food spoil unnoticed. Creative recycling of leftovers, freezing, and serving smaller portions also directly reduce the amount of food landing in the trash. What does remain after all (e.g., vegetable peelings) can be returned to nature through composting.\n\nThe incorrect answer: promotions and "unmissable" discounts often encourage impulse buying. If we stockpile food in bulk that we actually do not have time to consume before it spoils, we are not preventing waste, but rather increasing it further.

KvizK04=Around 1.3 billion tons of food are wasted globally each year (plus another 1.2 billion tons on farms), and food waste accounts for nearly 10 percent of man-made greenhouse gas emissions. What are the most effective governmental, regulatory, and commercial measures to systematically reduce food waste?

KvizK04V5=Applying immediate and significant price reduction strategies for near-expiry products: stores should use automated inventory management systems to identify and drastically discount goods close to their expiration date.

KvizK04V7=Supporting the disposal of expired or surplus food: the government should encourage stores to clear out surplus as quickly as possible (e.g., into municipal waste), thereby facilitating logistics and cleaning.
KvizK04V8=Mandating compulsory and transparent corporate waste data reporting: the government should require major food chains to publicly report the exact amount of food waste generated and discarded annually.
KvizK04V9=Financing regular and comprehensive national awareness-raising campaigns: ministries of education and consumer protection offices should provide ongoing public information from state funds regarding conscious shopping and storage.
KvizK04M=Reducing systemic food waste depends on legislation and market processes rather than individual habits alone.\n\nThe largest amount of food can be saved from the trash through coordinated steps by governments, authorities, and retail chains.\n\nThe key to the solution is penalizing waste, facilitating donations, and easing strict rules (e.g., aesthetic expectations, rigid expiration dates).\n\nThe incorrect answer is flawed because dumping surplus into municipal waste wastes resources and burdens the environment; the goal is to prevent waste generation or utilize it (e.g., food donation, composting).

KvizK07M=In debates about everyday energy conservation, turning off lights and standby mode often take center stage. Our individual decisions—from buying local products to choosing building materials—are capable of mitigating the massive energetic pressure on nature at a systemic level.\n\nThe incorrect answer: Why is buying disposable products for convenience wrong?\n\nThis behavior is the worst form of the "linear economy" (buy, use, throw away). The production of single-use products consumes a lot of energy and raw materials while serving for only a few minutes, then burdens the planet as waste that takes centuries to decompose. This mentality directly accelerates the crossing of sustainability boundaries.\n\nFrom a financial standpoint: the cheapest disposable products are the ones that instantly become the most expensive when we have to throw them away right after use—we have wasted our money on them needlessly.

KvizK08M=The Earth’s forests cannot be saved solely through individual good deeds, as destruction is driven by massive political, legal, and macroeconomic processes.\n\nExplanation of correct answers:\n\n- Legislation such as the European Union Deforestation Regulation cuts off the market for products from illegal or destructive sources, making global trade economically invested in sustainability.\n- Scientific research proves that deforestation rates are lowest in territories managed by indigenous peoples. KvizK13M=The fight against global warming and species extinction is not just the privilege of those living in houses with gardens. However, using synthetic chemicals and fertilizers damages the microenvironment and increases the ecological footprint of the chemical industry, making this method contrary to sustainability. Change starts with our individual actions even within the walls of our apartment!\n\nLet’s grow microgreens on the balcony!\n\nThe most popular, easiest to grow, and fast-developing indoor microgreens include: cress, radish, pea, sunflower, broccoli, mustard, arugula, and red cabbage.\nPopular, valuable herbs include: basil, cilantro, dill, parsley, and anise.\n\nAn insect/wasp hotel is one of the most useful urban biodiversity-boosting tools.\n\nResidents’ fear is entirely understandable, but it is based on a huge misunderstanding. The name can be very misleading. Aggressive social wasps living in colonies and acting as nuisances during summer cookouts (like yellowjackets) never move into insect hotels. They build large, paper-like nests in attics or underground holes. Insect hotels are used exclusively by solitary bees (e.g., mason bees) and solitary wasps. They have no queen, no colony, and do not defend a shared nest. There is no stinger danger—these insects are infinitely peaceful. They would only sting if someone literally squeezed them with a finger. They are completely harmless to humans or pets.\n\nWhy is an insect hotel very useful?\n\n- Attracts super-pollinators: Solitary bees are much more efficient pollinators than honeybees. A single mason bee visits thousands of flowers a day on balconies and in parks.\n\n- Natural pest control: Solitary wasps hunt aphids, caterpillars, and mosquito larvae to feed their sealed-in eggs inside the hotel. This cleans balcony plants of pests for free.\n\n- Green corridors: In a concrete jungle, insects cannot find natural bored holes or rotting wood for reproduction. An insect hotel placed on a balcony is a tremendous help to them in the middle of the city.

KvizK27=If humanity is unwilling to eliminate its dependence on fossil fuels, the collapse of the polar ice sheets and catastrophic sea level rise could only be slowed down by radical and risky technological interventions (geoengineering). Which of the following astonishing, but in reality planned or tested global engineering projects are proposed by researchers as a last resort to save the Arctic and Antarctic ice?
KvizK27V1=Construction of underwater marine curtains and dams: 80-kilometer-long, flexible physical barriers anchored to the seabed would be erected in front of vulnerable glaciers to divert deep-flowing warm ocean waters that melt the ice blocks from below.
KvizK27V2=Stratospheric aerosol injection (sulfur dioxide): introducing sulfur dioxide into the upper atmosphere via airplanes or balloons to mimic the effect of giant volcanic eruptions, creating a kind of global parasol that would directly cool the polar regions.
KvizK27V3=Iron fertilization of polar oceans: scattering tons of iron sulfate powder into the open sea to induce artificial algal blooms that absorb CO2 and then sink to the seabed along with the dead algae.
KvizK27V4=Artificial microbubble foaming of ocean surfaces: using special ships or additives to pump billions of microscopic air bubbles into the sea to turn the dark ocean surface milky white and highly reflective over vast areas.
KvizK27V5=Spreading glass microspheres on the ice: scattering millions of tons of microscopic, hollow, reflective glass spheres onto the surface of the polar ice to artificially increase the ice’s reflectivity (albedo) against summer sunlight.
KvizK27V6=Marine cloud brightening with salt spray: using automated ship fleets to spray salty seawater into the clouds above the polar oceans to make them denser and whiter, thereby reflecting much more sunlight back into space.
KvizK27V7=Covering icebergs and glaciers with a giant aluminum foil layer: covering all melting glaciers, as well as the ice sheets of Greenland and Antarctica, with white textile tarpaulins and metallic aluminum foil to reduce their melting.
KvizK27V8=Industrial pumping of subglacial meltwater: drilling thousands of deep boreholes through the ice sheets to pump out the meltwater between the ice and the bedrock, which acts as a slippery lubricant accelerating the glaciers’ slide into the ocean.
KvizK27V9=Pumping seawater onto ice in winter: installing thousands of wind-powered pumps on the polar ice to pump seawater to the surface during the freezing winter months, allowing it to freeze and artificially thicken the protective ice layer.
KvizK27M=The greatest climate dilemma of the modern era: if we do not reduce fossil emissions, we will be forced to resort to the drastic and dangerous manipulation of nature. All of the correct answers are real scientific proposals or experiments.\n\nThe list is perfect proof of the principle that "the medicine is sometimes more dangerous than the disease itself." Geoengineering does not solve the root cause of climate change (CO2 emissions), it merely provides symptomatic treatment, while according to researchers analyzing the projects in detail, each method is an ecological time bomb.\n\nIron fertilization, for instance, has already been tested several times in polar waters, but it turned out that the algal bloom (the drastically multiplying algae) deprives deep-sea life of oxygen, creating anoxic death zones. Similarly, ocean microbubble foaming would blind marine wildlife, while sulfur powder would destroy the ozone layer and could cause global droughts.\n\nInstead of "hacking" the planet, eliminating hydrocarbon dependence is the only safe path to curb the melting of polar ice sheets, stop sea-level rise, and ultimately mitigate global warming.\n\nA brief overview of the projects included in the quiz, which clearly demonstrates the severe environmental and physical risks behind each method:\n\n- Construction of underwater marine curtains and dams\nThe risk: Gigantic physical barriers anchored to the seabed could completely disrupt polar ocean currents and alter nutrient cycling. This would have a catastrophic impact on local marine ecosystems, cutting off deep-sea organisms from the food necessary for their survival. Furthermore, their implementation carries unforeseeable logistical and engineering hazards in freezing, stormy waters.\n\n- Stratospheric aerosol injection (sulfur dioxide)\nThe risk: Artificially introducing sulfur dioxide into the atmosphere could severely damage the protective ozone layer and cause global acid rain. Yet its greatest danger is that it alters global precipitation patterns, which could induce killer droughts and famine in Asia and Africa. Moreover, if the system is once started and then suddenly stopped (for instance, due to war or a technical failure), the ice sheets could experience a devastating "termination shock," bringing immediate, explosive global warming.\n\n- Iron fertilization of polar oceans\nThe risk: Artificial algal blooms triggered by iron powder consume all the oxygen in the water when the algae die and begin to decompose. This creates vast, lifeless dead zones in the ocean, destroying fish and polar marine wildlife. In certain cases, the method could also favor the proliferation of algae species producing neurotoxins that poison whales and polar birds.\n\n- Artificial microbubble foaming of ocean surfaces\nThe risk: Turning the sea surface milky white and highly reflective with microbubbles blocks sunlight from marine plants and plankton. Since plankton form the absolute foundation of the oceanic food chain and produce a significant portion of Earth’s oxygen, prolonged darkness could cause the collapse of the entire marine ecosystem. The dense foam layer would also inhibit natural gas exchange between the ocean and the atmosphere.\n\n- Spreading glass microspheres on the ice\nThe risk: Independent computer modeling has revealed that microscopic glass spheres do not work properly on all ice types. On certain polar ice surfaces, the spheres actually absorb heat, darkening the surface and turning out exactly the opposite way: accelerating ice melt. Additionally, littering the polar ecosystem with microscopic glass grains would cause unforeseeable damage to the bodies of animals living there.\n\n- Marine cloud brightening with salt spray\nThe risk: Brightening clouds with salt crystals drastically interferes with regional meteorology. According to research, this method could reduce the natural amplitude of the El Nino (ENSO) climate phenomenon by up to 60 percent, making global weather completely unpredictable. This drastic change could trigger sudden and devastating floods or extreme droughts in distant parts of the world, completely ruining agriculture.\n\n- Industrial pumping of subglacial meltwater\nThe risk: To pump water out from under the glaciers, thousands of kilometers of deep boreholes would need to be drilled through the moving, unstable ice sheets. This massive industrial intervention could physically destabilize the ice structure, cause cracks, and lead to the ice sheet breaking into pieces and sliding into the ocean even faster, instead of the expected slowdown.\n\n- Pumping seawater onto ice in winter\nThe risk: During the process of pumping seawater to the surface, the high salt concentration entering the snow destroys the snow’s natural, clean reflectivity (albedo). When the polar summer arrives, this salty ice layer will absorb all heat much faster than normal snow, accelerating summer melting. Furthermore, the noise and environmental pollution from millions of machines operating in polar landscapes would drive away protected animals like polar bears.\n\nThe incorrect answer:\n\n- Covering glaciers with aluminum foil\nAlthough smaller glaciers in the Alps are indeed covered with special white textile tarpaulins during summer, covering the continuously moving ice sheets of Greenland and Antarctica—spanning millions of square kilometers—with metallic aluminum foil would be a physically unfeasible, polluting misconception, and no scientific institute proposes such a project.\nThe risk: Although it is clearly an unfeasible theory, its physical and environmental risks would also be immense. The metallic foil layers would reflect heat but would completely cut off the ice surface from the air, destroying the unique microorganisms (e.g., cryophilic algae) living on the ice. Stormy polar winds would tear the foil into pieces, and the billions of metal and plastic debris fragments would irreversibly poison polar waters and wildlife.\n\n+1 Theory not included in the quiz, which was already in an advanced stage of planning and testing but was ultimately discarded:\n\n- Spraying chalk powder into the atmosphere (SCoPEx project): Spraying calcium carbonate (fine chalk powder) into the stratosphere to reflect solar radiation. This was an official experimental project of Harvard University, which ultimately had to be halted due to severe ethical and environmental concerns, as well as immense international outcry. When they attempted to conduct the first live test in northern Sweden in 2021, the local indigenous Sami community and environmentalists vetoed it.\n\nResearchers modeled the potential drawbacks of the technology in detail:\n\n- Unexpected chemical reactions in the stratosphere: Although chalk powder (calcium carbonate) is a natural and harmless substance on the Earth’s surface, it behaves quite differently in the upper atmosphere (the stratosphere). Computer models showed that chalk-bearing aerosols could chemically react with other gases in the atmosphere (such as volcanic sulfuric acid or man-made chlorine compounds). This process could accelerate the depletion of the protective ozone layer, allowing more harmful UV radiation to reach the Earth’s surface, thereby increasing the risk of skin cancer and damaging plant life.\n- Disruption of global weather systems: Artificially reflecting solar radiation through chalk powder reduces the energy reaching the surface, which alters global atmospheric currents. This drastic temperature modification could disrupt monsoons and global rainfall patterns. Consequently, the method could cause catastrophic droughts in the world’s most populous agricultural regions (such as South Asia and parts of Africa), endangering the food security of millions.\n- Geopolitical conflicts and the danger of a "weather weapon": Since the atmosphere is a unified system, unilateral action by a country or a research group impacts the weather of the entire planet. If a nation (or a billionaire private investor) sprays chalk powder into the atmosphere to cool its own region, and because of this, the harvest in a neighboring country is ruined due to drought, it could lead to international conflicts or even wars. Currently, there is no global legal framework or governmental consensus to decide who gets to control the "planet’s thermostat."\n- The "termination shock": If humanity does not stop burning fossil fuels and masks warming exclusively through the continuous dusting of the atmosphere with chalk powder, it traps itself. If the system had to be suddenly shut down due to war, technical disaster, or political crisis, the ice sheets and the planet would experience a devastating heat shock. Due to the greenhouse gases accumulated over decades, the global temperature could jump several degrees Celsius in just a few years, causing an immediate and irreversible climate catastrophe.\n- Moral hazard: According to opponents of the project, the mere act of experimenting creates a false illusion among politicians and large corporations that climate change can be solved with a cheap technological trick. This diverts attention and resources away from the real solution—phasing out coal, oil, and gas—causing humanity to delay real action until it is too late.

KvizK28V9=You prioritize restaurants and shops that have official, transparent procedures for sourcing seafood from sustainable origins.
KvizK28M=The correct answers: these are the direct consumer decisions and indirect supportive activities recommended for individuals by international environmental organizations. At the top of the list is exerting direct market pressure (looking for certifications and reducing consumption).\n\nThe incorrect answer: bulk purchasing of cheap, discounted sea fish in reality achieves the exact opposite effect. In the fishing industry, low prices almost always mask unsustainable, destructive practices (e.g., illegal fishing, slave labor, or environmental degradation). High-volume purchasing does not stop overproduction; instead, it generates continuous profit for companies, thereby increasing demand for overfished stocks.\n\nWhy does individual responsibility matter?\n\nAlthough overfishing is a global, industrial-scale problem, its engine is driven by everyday consumer demand. Every time we buy or order fish, we make a choice: we support the plunder of the seas or we stand by sustainable solutions. Conscious purchasing (such as choosing certified products), moderating consumption, and supporting environmental organizations exert direct market and social pressure on the fishing industry and decision-makers.\n\nThe future of the seas begins on our plates.

KvizK29=Which individual decisions, daily hygiene habits, and responsible behaviors allow you to most effectively prevent the emergence or global spread of another pandemic at an individual level?
KvizK29V1=Routine application of thorough handwashing with soap, hand sanitizing, and coughing etiquette (coughing into a tissue or the crook of your elbow).
KvizK29V2=Immediate voluntary isolation (staying home) in case of respiratory or infectious symptoms, avoiding workplace/school communities, and wearing a mask if necessary.
KvizK29V3=Respecting the natural habitats of wild animals, and avoiding keeping exotic animals as pets or consuming wild meat, thereby minimizing the risk of dangerous zoonoses (infections transmitted from animals to humans).
KvizK29V4=Consciously reducing our meat and dairy consumption and prioritizing plant-based alternatives, thereby individually decreasing global demand for crowded industrial livestock farms and slaughterhouses, which are considered breeding grounds for viruses.
KvizK29V5=Deliberately visiting enclosed, crowded places (e.g., cinemas, malls) even with infectious symptoms to quickly achieve community immunity so that everyone gets over the illness as soon as possible.
KvizK29V6=Checking the epidemiological situation of the destination country before traveling abroad, and voluntary quarantine or testing upon returning home, since globalization and air travel can turn a local virus into a global one within hours.
KvizK29V7=Regular, cross-ventilated airing of indoor spaces at home and in workplaces, which drastically reduces the concentration of airborne pathogens.
KvizK29V8=Strictly adhering to antibiotics and antiviral drugs prescribed by a doctor, avoiding unnecessary or discontinued medication use, which can lead to the emergence of incurable superbugs.
KvizK29V9=Getting recommended basic and seasonal vaccinations, which protect not only us but also vulnerable groups in our environment through herd immunity.
KvizK29M=Explanation of correct answers:\n\n- Mechanical cleaning and hand hygiene represent the very first and cheapest line of defense to physically halt pathogens.\n- If someone feels ill and stays home, they individually break the chain of infection, preventing themselves from becoming a "superspreader."\n- The majority of new pandemics are of animal origin (zoonoses). Our individual decisions—such as leaving wildlife alone and rejecting illegal wildlife trade—directly prevent unknown viruses from jumping to humans.\n- Curbing industrial meat consumption reduces the volume of factory farming, giving viruses fewer chances to mutate and spread explosively in enclosed spaces. Intensive livestock farming has been classified as a global health hazard because it favors the development of antibiotic-resistant pathogens due to farming and processing conditions, as well as continuous human-animal contact.\n- In the modern world, mobility is the engine of pandemics. The awareness and discipline of travelers determine whether a local outbreak remains contained or escalates into a pandemic.\n- Ventilating enclosed spaces is one of the most effective individual methods to dilute the concentration of respiratory viruses spread via droplets.\n- If we do not complete the full course of antibiotics, surviving pathogens mutate. Improper medication use can trigger a global resistance crisis and a new, aggressive pandemic.\n- Getting vaccinated reduces the mutation chances of viruses, as the pathogen finds it much more difficult to multiply and change within a protected organism.\n\nThe incorrect answer: Deliberately spreading illnesses leads to an uncontrollable surge in case numbers. This immediately collapses the healthcare system and drastically increases the mortality rate.\n\nPreventing the next pandemic depends not only on laboratories and government decisions but also on our daily choices. According to modern science, most pandemics spill over from animals to humans (zoonoses), a risk drastically amplified by deforestation, the disruption of wildlife, and our massive global demand for crowded factory farming. When we reduce our meat consumption or respect nature, we handle the root of the problem directly.\n\nIf a virus does emerge, globalized air travel means it can circle the Earth in hours. This is when our second line of defense comes into play: conscious travel, ventilating enclosed spaces, thorough handwashing, and disciplined staying at home when showing symptoms. The key to prevention is responsible individual behavior—while intentional infection (the flawed answer) causes the collapse of healthcare rather than immunity.

KvizK30=Which of the following are effective systemic measures and practices to avoid waste and overconsumption, helping humanity remain within sustainability boundaries?
KvizK30V1=Circular economic regulation: introducing laws that obligate manufacturers to manage the full life cycle of products and ensure recycling.
KvizK30V2=Environmental tax reform: taxing raw material extraction and pollution while reducing the burdens on green technologies.
KvizK30V3=Banning planned obsolescence: applying strict legal sanctions against manufacturers of electronic and consumer goods designed with a deliberately short lifespan.
KvizK30V4=Developing green infrastructure and public transit: massive state investments in renewable energy and affordable, carbon-neutral public transport.
KvizK30V5=Strict packaging and waste management laws: completely banning single-use plastics and mandating support for package-free solutions.
KvizK30V6=Educational reform and awareness raising: making sustainability and systems thinking mandatory in the national core curriculum starting from the lowest grades.
KvizK30V7=Maximalizing GDP growth at all costs: exclusively measuring economic success through the continuous increase of consumption, regardless of its environmental impacts.
KvizK30V8=Eco-labeling and transparency obligations: introducing a unified, mandatory state labeling system to indicate the carbon footprint and repairability of products.
KvizK30V9=Supporting local food chains: providing subsidies to local farmers, thereby reducing waste and environmental burdens stemming from global transport.
KvizK30M=Crossing sustainability boundaries cannot be prevented through individual goodwill alone. It is the task of governments to create legal and economic ground rules that make sustainable choices cheaper and more accessible. Circular regulations, green taxes, and banning planned obsolescence force corporations into responsible operations, while infrastructure development (e.g., public transit) lays the foundation for green alternatives.\n\nThe incorrect answer: Why is maximizing GDP growth at all costs wrong?\n\nTraditional GDP measures solely the volume of production and consumption in monetary terms. If a country cuts down all its forests to manufacture furniture, its GDP will increase while its environmental systems collapse. Chasing growth while ignoring the fineness of natural resources is the main engine of overconsumption.

KvizK31=Which of the following are effective everyday practices belonging to personal responsibility that allow you to avoid waste and overconsumption, helping yourself and humanity remain within sustainability boundaries?
KvizK31V1=Conscious reduction of consumption and waste: evaluating your real needs and desires before purchasing, avoiding impulse buying and the accumulation of excess, and striving to use existing items until the end of their lifespan.
KvizK31V2=Practice of repair and reuse: repairing or having broken things (tools, clothes, appliances) repaired instead of throwing them away, buying second-hand goods whenever possible, and gifting, selling, or donating your unnecessary but still usable items.
KvizK31V3=Prioritizing a plant-based, local diet: significantly reducing the consumption of meat and dairy products, and choosing seasonal, local food originating from sustainable sources.
KvizK31V4=Minimizing food waste: consciously planning menus, writing precise shopping lists, creatively utilizing leftovers, and composting what is possible.
KvizK31V5=Reviewing household appliances regarding obsolescence: immediately replacing every working but older household appliance with the newest eco-labeled model.
KvizK31V6=Choosing sustainable modes of transport: walking, cycling, riding a scooter, or regularly using public transportation instead of driving.
KvizK31V7=Energy and water conservation in your home: optimizing heating/cooling, turning off standby modes, and using energy-saving appliances and water-saving fixtures.
KvizK31V8=Quality over quantity: buying durable, ethically sourced fashion items and clothes (slow fashion) instead of rapidly changing, cheap, and disposable fashion products (fast fashion).
KvizK31V9=Supporting the sharing economy: renting or borrowing tools (e.g., implements, cars) instead of purchasing your own for everything.
KvizK31M=Alongside systemic changes, a significant portion of global emissions and waste stems from the direct decisions of households.\n\nThe most critical step is consciously curbing consumption—meaning not buying what is not needed (a major part of which is avoiding impulse buying driven by promotions and "unmissable" discounts)—followed by extending the lifespan of our existing things (repair, reuse). Altering dietary habits (less meat), curbing food waste, and moderating car use carry the largest direct positive environmental impact at an individual level.\n\nExplanation of the incorrect answer: although using energy-efficient appliances is eco-friendly, immediately discarding still-functioning or repairable devices and buying new ones increases overconsumption and generates massive amounts of electronic waste. Ultimately, by constantly purchasing modern "eco-labeled" products, we fall into the trap of a superficial green solution because this also generates overconsumption. Their manufacturing and transport entail an enormous environmental burden, so replacing still-working devices actually does more harm than good. The most sustainable appliance is always the one that is already manufactured and in use.\n\nAn example:\n\n- The hidden environmental burden: manufacturing a single new smartphone or household appliance requires mining rare earth elements and raw materials from various parts of the world (such as Congo or Chile).\n- The manufacturing footprint: approximately 70–80 percent of an electronic device’s full life-cycle carbon footprint is linked to the manufacturing and transport itself, rather than subsequent home use.\n- The conclusion: keeping an older appliance that consumes slightly more electricity almost always represents a smaller burden on nature than having a brand-new, energy-efficient appliance manufactured and shipped home.\n\nSustainability hierarchy: the question is built upon the most crucial principle of environmental protection, according to which the most valuable step is prevention (not buying new), followed by reuse and repair, and only at the very end comes recycling.\n\nThe order of importance (the 3R principle - Reduce, Reuse & Repair, Recycle):\n\nStep 1: Reduce! – This is the most important. If you do not even purchase the unnecessary product, no raw materials need to be mined for it, and no manufacturing carbon dioxide is generated.\nStep 2: Reuse and repair! – This extends the lifespan of already existing items, thereby delaying the moment when new ones would need to be manufactured in their place.\nStep 3: Recycle! – Although important, recycling also requires a lot of energy, and the quality of materials often degrades during the process. Therefore, this is not the main solution, but the absolute last resort.\n\nUltimately, by directly cutting back consumption and extending the lifespan of objects, we extract the least amount of energy and raw materials from nature—which is one of the important cornerstones of the emerging circular economy.

FenntartK01=You’re sitting in a restaurant, or at a self-service buffet restaurant. Considering sustainability, choose the correct actions!

That way you don’t need the restaurant’s napkin—or if it’s already on your table, you can keep it as a memento (or use it later). FenntartK03=To reduce environmental problems, we need to cut back—among other things—on meat consumption. Select the actions that can help if you can’t give up meat!

FenntartK04=You’re about to shop online. Which considerations and practices do you follow if you want to procure the desired products consciously and sustainably?

FenntartK04V04=You support manufacturers who prioritize quality and make their products (and packaging) as recyclable as possible.
FenntartK04V05=When buying, packaging matters too: it should be made from recycled material, with as little filler as possible.

FenntartK04V12=You only order online after confirming the product isn’t available locally from sellers carrying nearby companies’ products.
FenntartK04V13=You order from companies that operate with the shortest possible supply chain—because it matters to you that the product reaches you with the smallest environmental burden.
FenntartK04M=Make considered decisions when shopping online—think carefully about what you order and have delivered.\n\nDon’t order more sizes or types than necessary just because you hope one will fit.\n\nFor clothing, choose the exact size; in general, choose good quality for every product.\n\nUnnecessary shipping wastes energy and causes extra greenhouse-gas emissions, and some returns end up as trash.\n\nWhy?\n\nBecause it’s not always economical for sellers to inspect, clean, and re-package returns, and warehouse rentals are expensive.\n\nDon’t head out yourself to pick up the package—have it sent to a nearby pickup point or your address.\n\nUsing shortest-route algorithms, couriers can make many deliveries per day—far more cost- and energy-efficient (and with far less pollution) than everyone fetching their own parcels.

FenntartK05M=To keep our future livable, it’s essential to reduce pollution generated around us.\n\nTrash and waste are part of this, because once in nature they contaminate soil, air, and water, and we cannot fully recycle the huge volumes of waste we generate.\n\nBurning or landfilling waste is extremely wasteful: it not only pollutes our environment, it squanders the energy and raw materials used to make products and forecloses the chance to recycle valuable materials.\n\nIf you must buy plastic packaging, always check its code.\n\n- Recyclable (and collected selectively): PETE or PET (polyethylene terephthalate) (1), PP (polypropylene) (5), HDPE (high-density polyethylene) (2), and LDPE (low-density polyethylene) (4).\n\n- Not, or only with difficulty, recyclable: PVC (polyvinyl chloride) (3), used in construction, medical, and automotive sectors; PS (polystyrene—its foamed form is Styrofoam) (6), used for insulation, cladding, and food containers; and “Other” (7), which covers all plastics not listed above (e.g., PC—polycarbonate).\n\nPlastics labeled 3, 6, or 7 are not collected selectively; depending on type and composition, they’re often recyclable only in costly, energy-intensive ways, and some variants fall entirely outside recyclable categories, often due to toxic content or effects—avoid them.

FenntartK08=Select the household activities that reduce your drinking-water use and wastewater generation!
FenntartK08V01=With lower water use, a modern water- and energy-saving dishwasher is more efficient than hand-washing—but only if you run it full and choose a short program at a moderate temperature.
