FenntartK08V11=You install water-saving aerators (nozzles that mix air into the water) on taps and/or use sensor faucets (the water flows only while your hands are underneath).
FenntartK08V12=You water garden or house plants less often and with less water, and you place all houseplants in the shade so their water demand is lower.
FenntartK08V13=While washing dishes, you turn off the tap while you scrub with the sponge, using running water only to fill the sink and to rinse the dishes.
FenntartK08M=Clean drinking water is our most valuable natural resource.\n\nThere are countless household practices to keep drinking water clean and to reduce consumption—look them up and apply as many as you can.\n\nAlso drink plenty of water; it’s a key pillar of health.\n\nWater your garden and houseplants properly, but avoid overwatering.\n\nDon’t forget the wildlife around you (birds, insects, and other animals living near your home): put out drinkers filled with fresh water in your garden or on your terrace, and if possible create a garden pond.\n\nIf tap water is of good quality, don’t choose bottled water—this also reduces plastic use. If you don’t like the taste of tap water, get a simple water filter or a bottled-water dispenser.\n\nIf you’re thinking about buying clothes, opt for good-quality second-hand items instead of new ones, and eat less meat and more plant foods.\n\nThe fashion industry and industrial meat production both consume vast amounts of water; by buying fewer new clothes and switching to a plant-forward diet you indirectly help reduce drinking-water use and wastewater generation.

FenntartK09=How can you save energy in the household? Select the relevant activities!
FenntartK09V01=You don’t leave your computer or TV running for hours unattended; you switch off unused lights; you don’t leave electronics in standby after shutdown; you unplug unused adapters.
FenntartK09V02=To boil 1–2 liters of water you use an electric kettle instead of a gas hob, and for boiling eggs you use an egg cooker—both are more energy-efficient than boiling in a pot.
FenntartK09V03=You wash clothes at the lowest temperature necessary for proper cleaning (most of the time 30–40 degrees Celsius is enough).
FenntartK09V04=In summer you dehumidify your home; with lower humidity the perceived temperature is lower and sweat evaporates faster, aiding cooling, so there’s no need to chill the air excessively—30 degrees Celsius can feel pleasant.
FenntartK09V05=You power remote controls and children’s electric toys with disposable batteries because they’re cheaper than buying more expensive, often rechargeable ones.
FenntartK09V06=You don’t use media devices simultaneously—no TV and hi-fi in the background while you game on a tablet and chat on your phone...
FenntartK09V07=Your fridge, freezer, washing machine, vacuum, and boiler are at least “A” energy class; your small kitchen appliances are durable and good quality.
FenntartK09V08=You use energy-saving light sources in every room, and low-consumption smart bulbs you can switch on/off from your phone or home controller.
FenntartK09V09=Outdoors you use lighting only when and as long as needed, with programmable, motion-sensing, and dimming solutions.
FenntartK09V10=You use an induction cooktop (more efficient and economical than gas), which saves energy because heat is generated only where the pot contacts the hob—the rest stays cool.
FenntartK09V11=If you need air conditioning, you choose an energy-saving inverter model (which can even heat below 0 degrees Celsius) and in summer you set it only 4–5 degrees Celsius cooler than outdoors so anyone coming in immediately feels comfortable.
FenntartK09V12=If you have AC, you clean it before both the cooling and heating seasons—important not only for bacteria and mold; dusty filters also reduce performance.
FenntartK09V13=You choose a water heater sized to your family’s hot-water needs and set the thermostat to pleasantly warm rather than hot so you don’t have to mix in cold water wastefully to make it usable.
FenntartK09M=Living consciously and energy-efficiently is good and important. There are many methods—big and small—to pursue an energy-saving lifestyle at home.\n\nEnergy saving doesn’t require giving things up; we just need to use generated energy more thoughtfully and deliberately. We can maintain comfort with more efficient energy use. An energy-saving lifestyle is not only cost-effective; it also reduces pressure on natural resources.\n\nMake sure your major appliances are “A” energy class—but because their full life cycle—manufacture, transport, operation, and end-of-life—demands resources and energy, you only use them sustainably if you operate them efficiently and avoid running them empty: freezers, dishwashers, washing machines, and dryers are most efficient when full (but not overfilled); for boilers, dishwashers, and washing machines choose operating water temperatures suited precisely to your needs, otherwise a lot of energy can be wasted.

FenntartK10=Transport and building heating are two major contributors to smog. By improving your home’s energy consumption, you can also cut the emissions associated with its operation. Select the applicable activities!
FenntartK10V01=You choose indoor temperatures wisely, knowing that a 1 degrees Celsius reduction yields about 6–7% energy savings.
FenntartK10V02=You insulate your home, install rooftop solar panels, heat with renewables, and modernize your heating system.
FenntartK10V03=You ensure radiators aren’t blocked by furniture or curtains, and you place aluminum foil or vapor-barrier heat-reflective foil behind them to radiate more heat into the room.
FenntartK10V04=At night you lower the shutters—improving insulation and reducing window condensation.
FenntartK10V05=Your home’s size matches the number of occupants—by choosing an optimally sized living space you reduce the building’s ecological footprint.
FenntartK10V06=You also insulate the roof and attic (large cooling surface in winter and warming surface in summer) and the basement ceiling if there’s a basement beneath the house.
FenntartK10V07=You invest in powerful AC units that cool in summer and heat in winter instead of insulating your home, considering this more cost- and energy-efficient.
FenntartK10V08=In a well-insulated house you don’t change the set temperature (e.g., when you go out), but you do set a few degrees lower in rarely used rooms.
FenntartK10V09=You check the insulation of windows and doors and, if needed, adjust the latch to pull the door tighter into the frame—heat stays in, dust, odors, and other pollutants stay out.
FenntartK10V10=If you have AC, you use it for heating at the start of the heating season, as this can be more economical than central heating.
FenntartK10V11=You improve indoor air quality not with windows left ajar for long periods (which cools walls and floors), but with short, intensive, wide-open ventilations.
FenntartK10V12=You keep the air moist (e.g., humidifier, aquarium, houseplants, a bowl with a damp sponge, water placed near a heat source), making the home feel warmer—while ensuring you don’t cause mold.
FenntartK10V13=You use a smart heating controller that optimizes your home’s temperature relative to outside conditions, saving 15–20% of heating energy.
FenntartK10M=Make your home “greener” and more environmentally friendly. Reducing your home’s energy consumption may mean extra costs, but it’s an investment that pays off.\n\nCooling and heating consume the most energy in households, so cutting them also lowers utility bills.\n\nIt also reduces the use of gas and oil, eases pressure on natural resources, and helps reduce human greenhouse-gas emissions.\n\nFor heat, it’s more economical to improve heat retention than heat production capacity.\n\nSo prioritize investments that preserve generated heat (e.g., better insulation) over those that only improve heating (e.g., heating modernisation).

FenntartK11=There are many ways to save energy—and money—at home. Select these activities!
FenntartK11V01=A lot of heat escapes through windows, so you install shutters and complement them with thick blackout curtains in winter.
FenntartK11V02=Instead of energy-intensive bottled waters and soft drinks in plastic bottles, you choose tap water, a reusable bottle, and homemade cordials—far more energy-efficient and almost zero waste.
FenntartK11V03=You mainly buy polyester (synthetic-fiber) clothing because it’s inexpensive and washing/drying it doesn’t pollute air and water.
FenntartK11V04=You use motion-sensing lighting anywhere light is only needed when someone is present (basement, entryway, terrace, etc.).
FenntartK11V05=Instead of waste-heavy plastic coffee capsules, you use refillable metal capsules or choose stovetop or grinder-based brewing.
FenntartK11V06=You banish space heaters and oil radiators by insulating your house.
FenntartK11V07=Before washing, you check worn clothes and, if they aren’t dirty—just used—you wash them at a lower temperature with less energy.
FenntartK11V08=You add rugs in rooms and living spaces—they need cleaning, but (if you don’t have underfloor heating) they reduce cold from the floor, make rooms cozier, and improve winter comfort.
FenntartK11V09=Instead of a desktop you invest in a modern laptop—smaller footprint, easier to move and transport, and much lower energy consumption.
FenntartK11V10=Icing and running a fridge/freezer nearly empty lowers efficiency—the food inside also holds the cold, which improves efficiency.
FenntartK11V11=You organize a garage sale or list still-good items online—what you don’t need may be a treasure for someone else.
FenntartK11V12=You switch off the oven a few minutes before the end—behind a closed door it cools slowly and the food finishes cooking with less energy.
FenntartK11V13=You swap forgotten, outgrown, or unused clothes with friends so both sides can get valuable pieces—better than filling the attic.
FenntartK11M=The main principle of energy saving is to use only as much energy as is absolutely necessary—where, when, and to the extent it’s needed.\n\nUse efficient systems and devices to burden your environment as little as possible.\n\nBuy durable, good-quality items—when you no longer need them, they can be passed on to others.\n\nThis applies to clothing, too—choose natural fibers and avoid synthetics, as the latter’s production, cleaning, recycling, disposal—and release into nature—carry heavier environmental burdens.\n\nThough hard to avoid polyester clothes, strive to: during washing and tumble-drying, microplastics released from them seriously pollute air and water.

FenntartK12=There are many ways to cut energy use at home, which—depending on how energy is produced—can also improve air quality. Select the correct activities!
FenntartK12V01=After single-use items wear out you replace them with durable, washable, many-times-reusable versions—saving a lot of money and energy and generating far less waste.
FenntartK12V02=By using shading, an awning above windows, and by consciously choosing the species and placement of garden trees you reduce summer AC use;
FenntartK12V03=You support home heating with a programmable thermostat; with settings tailored to your needs you save energy if you’re away for days or at night when 1–2 degrees Celsius less is enough.
FenntartK12V04=You get a lower-consumption but still adequately powerful AC unit—reducing electricity use and CO2 emissions;
FenntartK12V05=After charging you unplug the phone and you switch off the TV and computer after use—the devices and power supplies remain plugged in, but no longer consume electricity.
FenntartK12V06=Instead of small desk fans you install ceiling fans—the air circulation makes summer heat more bearable and they consume much less energy than AC units.
FenntartK12V07=With a well-placed home wind turbine you can increase the share of electricity from renewables and further reduce the share from non-renewables.
FenntartK12V08=Like many store-bought goods, spices may reach you with a significant environmental burden—so you grow the most important culinary herbs in your garden or on the windowsill.
FenntartK12V09=You put kitchen green waste in a composter, not the general trash—you know compost becomes the most valuable soil amendment over time—for exactly 0 forints.
FenntartK12V10=When building a new house you consider a passive house—it has no active heating or cooling, yet with outstanding insulation, minimal heat losses, and maximal gains it produces more energy than it consumes.
FenntartK12V11=You support electric mobility: you get an electric car, scooter, or bicycle, ideally charging them from solar panels (but even better is everyday cycling and walking);
FenntartK12V12=Knowing energy production and consumption burden the planet, you consciously plant trees—they provide shade, remove heat, and help climate-control your garden and the planet.
FenntartK12V13=Sometimes you no longer know where to save, yet the utility bill is high—so you call in an energy expert to point out every device, spot, and issue where energy is leaking.
FenntartK12M=Global demand for fuels and electricity is growing year by year, increasing CO2 emissions and significantly impacting global warming.\n\nRein in your energy use to ease the increasingly extreme, intensifying symptoms of climate change!\n\nContribute to a more moderate-energy future!\n\nThere are many ways to manage energy better.\n\nAmong the right methods is unplugging all idle electronics—because when plugged in they draw small amounts of power (e.g., standby).\n\nA home can have many devices whose combined standby consumption adds up to a significant—and unnecessary—monthly cost.\n\nSo unplug unused devices or use switched power strips so one switch cuts power to everything plugged into that strip.

FenntartK13=There are plenty of energy-saving and energy-efficient opportunities at home. Select the activities that help!
FenntartK13V01=You don’t refrigerate foods that don’t need it; you don’t put hot food in the fridge; and you pre-cool food in the fridge before placing it in the freezer so freezing uses less energy.
FenntartK13V02=You use minimal-consumption LED strips in the kitchen, LED bulbs throughout the home, and cozy, extremely efficient light strings in the living room and bedroom.
FenntartK13V03=You drink tap water instead of bottled water—or filtered water if you don’t like the taste—or you get a simple water filter or a bottled-water dispenser.
FenntartK13V04=You use solar lamps not only outdoors—after they charge outside during the day you bring them in at night; they’re great for ambient light and reading.
FenntartK13V05=For dinners and evening chats you light candles instead of lamps—creating lovely mood and fragrance.
FenntartK13V06=You use switched and smart power strips; with the former you can cut power to all plugged-in devices with a single switch, with the latter you can schedule when devices receive power.
FenntartK13V07=If you feel cold at home, you put on a warm sweater, wrap up in a blanket, drink hot tea, hot chocolate, or mulled wine—and maybe you won’t need to turn up the thermostat...
FenntartK13V08=You make the most of natural light—open the curtains in the morning and turn on lights only when there’s no longer enough daylight.
FenntartK13V09=You choose light (the whiter the better) wall paint, because light walls reflect more light—rooms stay brighter even on overcast days.
FenntartK13V10=You regularly check the door seals of the fridge and freezer and you don’t leave the door open long—warm, humid air entering the unit raises consumption.
FenntartK13V11=You upgrade a poorly sealing front door and outdated, low-insulation windows—often key reasons for heat loss even when exterior insulation is good.
FenntartK13V12=If you’re away for shorter or longer periods, you switch off the heating and the water heater—you don’t heat an empty home and no hot water is needed if no one is there.
FenntartK13V13=Cold feet and hands greatly worsen perceived warmth, and cold enters easily through the feet—so if you don’t have underfloor heating or the floor is cold, you use rugs and wear warm slippers.
FenntartK13M=There’s a difference between energy saving and energy efficiency: the former targets reducing consumption (e.g., switching off all lights), the latter strives for better use of energy (e.g., replacing all bulbs with LEDs).\n\nEnergy saving means using current devices less, while efficiency optimizes processes so they require less energy (e.g., replacing a machine with a lower-consumption one).\n\nThey share a big payoff: besides saving money, both reduce energy waste and your carbon footprint, helping conserve dwindling raw materials and protect our environment—benefiting our children, future generations, and Earth’s flora and fauna.\n\nThese ideas apply especially to heating, which consumes most household energy.\n\nFor example, if you’re away for a longer period, don’t switch heating off completely—the re-heating can cost a lot of energy. You do best by turning the thermostat down by a little or a lot depending on how long you’ll be away.  If you travel for longer, set a setback/anti-freeze temperature.\n\nThe same goes for the water heater: if you’re away for days (or weeks), don’t turn hot water off entirely (it’s very inconvenient to have no hot water when you return), just lower the water-heater temperature.

FenntartK14=With a little attention you can save energy and water when doing laundry. Select the eco-conscious washing practices!
FenntartK14V01=You only use programs warmer than 30 degrees Celsius for truly dirty laundry, to remove bacteria, or to prevent odors forming in the machine.
FenntartK14V02=You don’t overload the washing machine; otherwise washing won’t be effective and you’ll need to rewash poorly cleaned clothes—wasting energy.
FenntartK14V03=You use a dryer only when, e.g., rainy weather prevents line-drying or when you need clothes quickly—otherwise you dry clothes on racks or a clothesline outdoors; this saves energy, clothes smell fresher, and crease less.
FenntartK14V04=You run long programs only when truly necessary—multi-hour, often high-temperature programs are typically not required and consume a lot of energy.
FenntartK14V05=You wait until you have a full load to avoid wasting water and energy—if you must wash a half load, you use a quick or ECO program.
FenntartK14V06=You soak very dirty or badly stained items before putting them in the machine—preventing a second wash if stains don’t come out.
FenntartK14V07=Instead of detergent you use an eco-friendly laundry egg plus laundry fragrance, and in the dryer you use dryer balls that separate items so hot air circulates better and drying is faster.
FenntartK14V08=You schedule all machine washing and drying for one day, back-to-back, so each subsequent load benefits from residual heat in the machine.
FenntartK14V09=When moving laundry from washer to dryer, you give each item a good shake so tangled clothes don’t prolong drying and don’t crease as much.
FenntartK14V10=For spinning you choose the higher 1200 rpm speed—this increases electricity use somewhat but helps protect clothes from creasing.
FenntartK14V11=You remove clothes from the dryer as soon as they are dry—many machines keep tumbling to prevent creasing, which uses unnecessary energy.
FenntartK14V12=You add only as much detergent as needed—overdosing won’t make clothes cleaner, but residue can build up inside the machine and reduce efficiency.
FenntartK14V13=If you need a new washing machine, you choose as high a rating as possible (ideally “A”), which runs more economically and is therefore kinder to the environment.
FenntartK14M=Laundry is a frequent task—often multiple times a week—so without enough attention it can waste a lot of money and energy.\n\nWith a little care you can cut both your water and electricity bills.\n\nOne of the most important steps is choosing the right temperature.\n\nWashing at 30 degrees Celsius instead of 40 degrees Celsius can save more than 50% energy; it also extends garment life and colors fade more slowly.\n\nWith typical use, it’s usually enough to wash only towels, bedding, and kitchen cloths at higher than 30 degrees Celsius.\n\nFew people maintain their washing machines, yet a dirty machine uses more water and energy—so it’s worth cleaning the inside periodically.\n\nWash reachable/removable parts (e.g., detergent drawer, door gasket), wipe the door and drum with a vinegar cloth, then run the machine empty on its hottest setting.\n\nYour machine will be clean and, in exchange for a single wash, it will run better and more economically for a long time.

FenntartK15=You can save a lot of energy and money when cooking and baking—often with just a little attention. Select the energy-moderate practices!
FenntartK15V01=Instead of boiling water on the stovetop, you use an electric kettle—it’s faster and more efficient—then pour the hot water into the pot for steaming or boiling. 
FenntartK15V02=You always use lids on pots while cooking—less evaporation, faster cooking, and more nutrients retained.
FenntartK15V03=You try to bake as many dishes as possible in one go in the oven—better use of space and heat.
FenntartK15V04=You often order ready-made meals—considering this more cost-effective and less wasteful than cooking yourself.
FenntartK15V05=You use appropriately sized pots and match them to the burner or hob—if the pot base overhangs the cooking zone, you just heat the surroundings needlessly.
FenntartK15V06=You choose the oven’s convection function—the circulating hot air shortens baking time and food cooks more evenly.
FenntartK15V07=You often use a pressure cooker—an energy-saving device that practically “cooks lunch by itself,” while locking in flavor and aroma.
FenntartK15V08=You use glass or ceramic cookware instead of metal trays in the oven—these materials retain heat better than metal and can be more efficient. 
FenntartK15V09=You boil only as much water as needed for the dish—boiling excess water wastes a lot of energy.
FenntartK15V10=You switch off the oven 5–10 minutes before the end and use the residual heat to finish cooking.
FenntartK15V11=You preheat the oven only when absolutely necessary—apart from cakes and leavened doughs, most dishes don’t require a preheated oven.
FenntartK15V12=For heating and cooking you also use the microwave—it’s faster than the oven because it reaches high temperatures quickly, and its smaller size focuses heat more directly on the food. 
FenntartK15V13=In the kitchen you focus on quick, easy-to-make, nutritious, healthy dishes instead of long-cooking and/or heavy meals;
FenntartK15M=Cooking and baking are everyday activities, so it’s easy to do them on “autopilot” with less attention.\n\nBecause they’re daily tasks, they’re exactly where you can waste—or save—a lot; often it just takes fine-tuning habits to make them more eco-conscious.\n\nTry not to cook every day. You can prepare food for several days—saving money and energy, and time in the kitchen.\n\nMany people often choose food delivery—it can diversify the diet and spare the effort of cooking, but meals cost far more than cooking at home; you can’t influence ingredient quality, sourcing, or preparation; delivery uses energy; and the packaging becomes your waste (whose production, recycling, or disposal also takes significant energy).

FenntartK16=Live more moderately with energy at home. Select the relevant points!
FenntartK16V01=You keep the cooktop and radiators clean—a dirty hob wastes energy; dust and grime in fins and gaps reduce a radiator’s heat output.
FenntartK16V02=You improve hot-water efficiency by insulating hot-water pipes—reducing heat loss in the pipe and avoiding unnecessary extra work by the water heater.
FenntartK16V03=You set 7 degrees Celsius in the fridge and −18 degrees Celsius in the freezer (the optimal setpoints)—colder settings don’t help food and only raise consumption.
FenntartK16V04=You clean windows regularly—rooms are brighter afterward, you can use natural light better, and you need less artificial lighting.
FenntartK16V05=You have a professional inspect the building’s electrical system—undersized wiring and poor connections can heat up and waste electricity.
FenntartK16V06=You don’t heat empty rooms, and you turn down thermostatic valves in rarely used rooms.
FenntartK16V07=If you’re cold on the sofa, you rearrange furniture—push the sofa to interior walls, not exterior ones, which are always colder.
FenntartK16V08=You keep the fridge and freezer well stocked (cooled food helps maintain temperature), and you regularly defrost the freezer and the fridge’s freezer compartment.
FenntartK16V09=You keep ideal temperatures: 20–22 degrees Celsius during the day, 19–20 degrees Celsius while sleeping, 22–23 degrees Celsius in the bathroom. 
FenntartK16V10=In summer, instead of running AC overnight, you leave the window open at night.
FenntartK16V11=Lamp shades and bulbs collect dust and grime and give less light—so you clean them occasionally.
FenntartK16V12=In the morning you fill the kettle completely and use it all day (reheating as needed) for your several daily cups of coffee or tea.
FenntartK16V13=You descale the electric water heater from time to time—limescale around the heating elements worsens efficiency; a water heater is energy-saving only if maintained.
FenntartK16M=Creating an energy-saving home and living sustainably pays multiple dividends: it helps your wallet and protects the environment when you use less energy.\n\nProper insulation and renewables do a lot, but there are also tricks that cost nothing and still save a lot.\n\nLook into these tips and apply them—and share your own money- and energy-saving tricks, too!

FenntartK17=A more sustainable life takes good ideas and intent. Select the points that help you run a more conscious household!
FenntartK17V01=You recover (i.e., compost) vegetable scraps instead of putting them in general trash—otherwise you’d increase production of methane, one of the most problematic greenhouse gases.
FenntartK17V02=You grow your own vegetables, fruits, herbs, and sprouts—taking steps toward self-reliance and reducing the environmental burden of transporting products.
FenntartK17V03=You consistently track the contents of your fridge and pantry, bring forward items that expire sooner, and avoid buying unnecessary stock.
FenntartK17V04=You prioritize plant-based solutions—with conscious planning all nutrients needed to build and maintain the human body can come from plant sources.
FenntartK17V05=For short-shelf-life, perishable foods you buy only as much as you truly need until the next shopping trip.
FenntartK17V06=You use durable packaging and storage—glass, cloth, cotton—and say no to single-use films, nets, plastic bags, and polystyrene trays destined for immediate disposal.
FenntartK17V07=You learn proper storage for fruits and vegetables, and you preserve older or surplus produce by canning, drying, or fermenting.
FenntartK17V08=You follow sales and buy a lot of cheap items, because even if you don’t use them all, you still come out ahead compared with buying fewer of the pricier ones (which would be used up).
FenntartK17V09=Demand shapes supply—as a conscious buyer you investigate how products are made, what raw materials they use, and how they’re transported, and you find sustainable shops, products, and manufacturers.
FenntartK17V10=With your purchases you support local producers’ markets, organic farms, shops carrying local products, and zero-waste stores.
FenntartK17V11=You accept cosmetically imperfect produce at the market or store—reducing food waste and producers’ losses.
FenntartK17V12=You quit ultra-processed ready-meals and instead prepare real food—more likely avoiding GM ingredients and unnecessary packaging.
FenntartK17V13=With your money you support fair-trade alternatives—they may lack organic certification yet be “cleaner,” with more ethical, sustainable, and planet-friendly production.
FenntartK17M=Your sustainability efforts usually help your wallet, too.\n\nEveryone is responsible for their own actions and decisions—make the right choices within your sphere.\n\nThe more of us who act thoughtfully and choose peaceful, low-impact options, the sooner a more conscious society can emerge.\n\nIf everything were ethical, exploitation-free, and environmentally friendly, life would be easier for us all.\n\nBut we’re not there yet. So we must inform ourselves about things that endanger our health and that of the planet.\n\nIf everyone did their part, our world could function far better and become more sustainable.

FenntartK18=Reducing food waste is a fundamental task. Fermentation (pickling) is an excellent method—select the relevant points!
FenntartK18V01=Alongside drying, salting, and smoking, it’s one of the oldest preservation methods—saving surplus harvests by souring them.
FenntartK18V02=It makes vegetables and fruits tasty and pleasantly flavorful; their vitamin and mineral content becomes more accessible and better utilized by the body.
FenntartK18V03=Fermentation is one of the most natural preservation methods because it uses environmental microbes—the beneficial bacteria on the surface of produce.
FenntartK18V04=Pickling saves many vegetables from the trash while treating natural resources gently—the process requires very little energy.
FenntartK18V05=The best produce for pickling is seasonal and, where possible, from the closest sources.
FenntartK18V06=Without a fridge or freezer it extends shelf life and makes produce easier to digest by breaking down bitter or hard-to-digest compounds plants use as pest defenses.
FenntartK18V07=You can speed up fermentation by placing the filled jar in the fridge from the start, because cold promotes fermentation.
FenntartK18V08=It encourages higher vegetable intake—pickles are more acceptable even to those who like vegetables less raw or cooked.
FenntartK18V09=High water content in ingredients is a plus—this medium supports rapid bacterial growth and ultimately yields moisture-rich foods.
FenntartK18V10=Everything prepared this way is also a nutrient that doesn’t poison the environment and doesn’t need to be produced again—and is completely zero-waste.
FenntartK18V11=Beyond vegetables, you need only water, a little non-iodized salt, flavoring spices—and a well-sealing jar, room temperature, and a spot protected from direct sunlight.
FenntartK18V12=It’s a great way to process quickly perishing vegetables—especially if you’re behind on using them or have more than you can eat fresh.
FenntartK18V13=Fresh vegetables soon lose quality, starting to wilt or rot—fermentation not only prevents spoilage, it can even enhance their nutritional value.
FenntartK18M=Fermentation is an ancient technique of preservation that has recently moved to the center of scientific and household interest.\n\nLactic fermentation is an old-new tool to stop (or at least reduce) food waste and it effectively supports a healthy, gut-friendly diet.\n\nFermented food is already pre-processed by bacteria involved in the process—so it’s very easy to digest and far more nutritious (some research suggests nearly a hundredfold) than without fermentation.\n\nFermentation makes produce rich in flavor and aroma, full of vitamins and minerals—and if you do it well—crisp yet easy to bite.\n\nWith the exception of high-protein foods, almost any plant can be soured; choose the firmer varieties, as very soft ones change texture more during fermentation.\n\nWell-fermented vegetables include cabbage, cucumbers, carrots, red onions, beets, Jerusalem artichokes, zucchini, and radishes; among fruits it’s worth experimenting with firmer apples (e.g., Jonathan).

FenntartK19=The kitchen is a key area for a more sustainable household. Select the relevant points!
FenntartK19V01=You cook your meals yourself, prefer seasonal local ingredients, and plan ahead—reducing environmental impact and supporting your family’s health.
FenntartK19V02=You sort household waste for recycling and compost organic kitchen scraps, later using the compost to improve soil for your plants.
FenntartK19V03=You get good-quality appliances and utensils so you don’t have to replace them often—reducing waste and saving money.
FenntartK19V04=Instead of paper towels you use cloth kitchen towels; instead of plastic sponges you choose cloth dishcloths or natural sponges (e.g., hemp, loofah, coconut fiber).
FenntartK19V05=You only get as many pots, containers, dishes, and kitchen gadgets as truly needed, considering family size and how much time you spend in the kitchen.
FenntartK19V06=You reduce water use by using the dishwasher sensibly and fitting water-saving faucets in both kitchen and bathroom.
FenntartK19V07=You “hate” the general trash can, so you don’t have one at all at home—instead you sort all waste for recycling.
FenntartK19V08=For dishwashing and home cleaning you use eco-friendly agents, preferably homemade.
FenntartK19V09=When shopping you aim to buy as little packaging waste as possible—choosing bulk options when you can and bringing cloth produce bags and a shopping tote.
FenntartK19V10=You know exactly why you’re going to the store—you don’t decide on the spot—avoiding unnecessary purchases and waste and paying less at the register.
FenntartK19V11=There’s no place for single-use products in your household—solutions are long-term alternatives to plastic items (straws, plates, cups, cutlery)—they already exist.
FenntartK19V12=For home storage you use jars and strong, durable boxes and crates made of recycled plastic and metal.
FenntartK19V13=You periodically review the fridge, freezer, and pantry—and you plan upcoming meals based on items that expire sooner or were bought earlier.
FenntartK19M=In a more sustainable household, you can meet your needs in ways that do not jeopardize future generations’ ability to meet their own.\n\nThis means that you need to pay attention equally to your environment, to animal and plant life, and to your fellow humans.\n\nBut you can spare not only your environment, but also your wallet if you think with sustainability in mind and establish new habits in your kitchen.\n\nUnfortunately, we are not yet at the point where the municipal bin can be banished from households—to achieve this we would often have to make “everything we own” reusable, washable, and cleanable in other ways—ultimately make them like new again and again to save them from being thrown away.\n\nToday our municipal bins still fill up with lots of single-use items (or, in the best case, with trash unsuitable for recycling): such as hygiene waste, one-way packaging that can’t go into the selective collector (e.g., empty plastic cheese or sauce tubes, salami casings), dirty paper napkins and paper towels, or the contents of an emptied vacuum cleaner bag, etc...\n\nTake a look into your municipal bin and continue the list.\n\nStrive to ensure that as little single-use waste and non-recyclable trash as possible ends up in your municipal bin, because after collection it is often incinerated or ends up swelling landfills.

FenntartK20=Baking soda (sodium hydrogen carbonate) can be considered an eco-friendly miracle substance in the household. Choose what it can be used for!
FenntartK20V01=Deodorizing—baking soda can absorb odors—therefore you put some in a small bowl, place it in the kitchen, next to the trash container, in the fridge, or in the car—and you neutralize the smells with it.
FenntartK20V02=Washing—you use baking soda when washing both white and colored clothes—it can remove the most stubborn stains and it also softens the water.
FenntartK20V03=Cleaning everywhere—in the kitchen or the bathroom you scrub the surfaces of appliances and counters with its diluted or acidic (mixed with lemon juice or vinegar) solution, which is suitable for removing almost any stain.
FenntartK20V04=Unclogging—you sprinkle a few tablespoons of baking soda into the clogged drain, then pour in a few glasses of vinegar and with this (repeating the process for tougher cases) you can eliminate the clog.
FenntartK20V05=Homemade weed control—you sprinkle weeds with baking soda in the cracks of the sidewalk, paving stones, or driveway—its high sodium content suppresses the weeds.
FenntartK20V06=Chemical-free mopping—you mop with two tablespoons of baking soda dissolved in a bucket of warm water, which yields results just as good as using store-bought chemicals.
FenntartK20V07=Removing discoloration—you remove food-caused discoloration from plastic containers by soaking them and leaving them in baking-soda water for a few hours.
FenntartK20V08=Cleaning sponges and cloths—you extend the life of cleaning tools by occasionally rinsing them with baking-soda water.
FenntartK20V09=Baking baked goods—by adding a little baking soda to the ingredients of cakes and pastries, it makes them light and airy, and the baked bread will also be lighter and more aerated.
FenntartK20V10=Textile cleaning—you sprinkle baking soda on a stain formed on the carpet or sofa, then spritz it with vinegar, leave it on until dry, then loosen with a brush and vacuum it up—this removes the stain.
FenntartK20V11=Oil and grease stains—baking soda is an effective degreaser; e.g., you sprinkle a little baking soda on an oil stain on clothing, leave it on briefly, then rub it off.
FenntartK20V12=Stubborn food residues—you soak a pan or pot containing burnt-on bits in baking-soda water (you can even bring it to a boil), so the burnt residue will come off more easily.
FenntartK20V13=Removing rust—you sprinkle a little baking soda on rust formed on your kitchen tools, then scrub with a wet sponge or toothbrush, which makes your tools like new and polishes them.
FenntartK20M="Use baking soda!"—our grandmothers say for almost every problem that can occur in the household.\n\nIndeed, baking soda has countless household uses: besides making cakes and pastries light and airy, it can be used as a mouthwash, tooth whitener, deodorant, odor neutralizer, air freshener, whitening agent, cleaner, silver polish, degreaser, wall crayon-mark remover, weed killer, or even a shoe freshener.\n\nIt also has advantages in health uses: it may help relieve heartburn and heal painful mouth ulcers, soothe itchy skin and sunburn, improve athletic performance, slow chronic kidney disease, and may even improve certain cancer treatments.\n\nUse baking soda in your household too!

FenntartK21=There are many factors in heating living spaces that help reduce heating costs, environmental impact, and energy consumption without reducing comfort. Choose these!
FenntartK21V01=You modernize your heating system to a heat pump, which is one of the most sustainable heating and cooling solutions with minimal electricity demand.
FenntartK21V02=You make sure that the temperature difference between heated and less-heated rooms is not more than 4 degrees, because this avoids the humidity of warm air condensing on cold walls and potentially causing mold.
FenntartK21V03=By inspecting and, if necessary, replacing the circulation pumps of the heating and hot water systems, you improve their efficiency, which contributes to lower electricity costs.
FenntartK21V04=Before the heating season starts, you check the pressure of the heating system, bleed the radiators if necessary, and fill the heating system according to the manufacturer’s instructions, thereby maintaining its efficiency.
FenntartK21V05=You have a professional perform the hydraulic balancing of the heating system, by which the heating energy will be distributed evenly throughout the house, reducing heating costs.
FenntartK21V06=In the evenings you lower the venetian blinds or the shutters, and draw the blackout curtains—this also helps keep the cold air out and the warm air in.
FenntartK21V07=The air heated by radiators rises, so in addition to insulating the facade you also ensure the roof is insulated.
FenntartK21V08=You set the temperature of the hot water storage (boiler) to at least 70 degrees, because this way you get hot water faster and energy efficiently for showering and cooking.
FenntartK21V09=Comfortable humidity is between 40 and 60 percent—you increase low humidity with humidifying solutions, and reduce high humidity by ventilating the rooms.
FenntartK21V10=To assess places in the house and garden that consume too much energy, you request a thermal camera inspection from an energy consulting company—the thermal images show where heat escapes.
FenntartK21V11=You keep the doors closed to the pantry, basement stairs, attic access, and rooms that are generally cooler, and you check the sealing of doors and windows.
FenntartK21V12=You refresh the air in rooms by large-area, short, intensive ventilation or cross-draught ventilation, not by windows left on tilt.
FenntartK21V13=Alongside radiators you also use surface and/or underfloor heating, because these do not take up space in the room and, due to their even heat emission, are very energy efficient.
FenntartK21M=In heating living spaces, environmental awareness has become a very important task for all of us—not only because of cost reduction, but also because—among other things—we must reduce the environmental burden of heating.\n\nThe most important conditions: modern thermal insulation, well-sealed doors and windows, a maintained heating system, and in general keeping the heat from heating inside the building as long as possible.\n\nA properly maintained heating system also includes the correct setting of heating control: in many homes the heating control is not optimally calibrated, as a result of which the system properly heats the rooms near the boiler, but the more distant ones not sufficiently.\n\nTherefore, rooms farther from the boiler need more energy, even though there is enough heating heat in the system.\n\nHydraulic balancing helps with this: the professional determines the heat demand of each room and sets the heating system so that the heating energy is distributed as evenly as possible in the house and the desired temperature is reached in every room.

FenntartK22=Water is our most valuable natural resource, so we must strive to use less drinking water and thereby generate less wastewater. Select the relevant points!
FenntartK22V01=You wash your car at a car wash, because compared to washing at home they operate with much more efficient water use and can properly channel water polluted with cleaning agents.
FenntartK22V02=You consume foods with a small water footprint, i.e., more vegetables and fruits, and less meat and chocolate.
FenntartK22V03=You replace your toilet tank with a modern flushing tank, which has a flush/stop function or dual flush—using either correctly can save a lot of drinking water.
FenntartK22V04=In the household most water goes to hygiene: laundry, showering, toothbrushing, and toilet flushing—so you buy water-saving appliances and accessories.
FenntartK22V05=You wash dishes under running water, because this way the dirt comes off the dishes faster and more thoroughly and they become cleaner.
FenntartK22V06=You have a urinal installed, which uses less water per flush; even more water-saving is the dry urinal, which operates without flushing.
FenntartK22V07=With touch-sensor faucets, cartridges that can only be turned to the stop against resistance, and nozzles that mix air into the water, you reduce the amount of water flowing from the tap.
FenntartK22V08=You buy fewer new clothes, you prefer second-hand clothing stores, thrift shops, and swapping clothes with acquaintances.
FenntartK22V09=You don’t pour paints, varnishes, and expired medicines down the drain or into the toilet; you take them to a collection point.
FenntartK22V10=You don’t have money for a water-saving toilet tank, so you reduce the water volume of a large flush by placing large, clean stones or a sealed bottle filled with water in the tank.
FenntartK22V11=You water your garden in the morning or evening (preferably with collected rainwater), not in the daytime heat—plants also prefer this and less of the water evaporates, thus it’s used better.
FenntartK22V12=You turn off the tap while shaving or brushing your teeth, with which you save 5–10 liters of drinking water per minute; instead of bathing in a tub you shower for at most 4–5 minutes, saving at least 50 liters of water.
FenntartK22V13=On meeting tables at home and at work you also place a water jug and glasses instead of bottles of mineral water—this reduces not only stocking up on mineral water produced with a lot of energy but also plastic use.
FenntartK22M=Increasing water use, population growth, and climate change may cause ever greater problems of water and energy scarcity, primarily in developing countries, but negative effects will be felt elsewhere too.\n\nTherefore we must handle water resources carefully and sparingly—according to research and forecasts, due to climate change, precipitation will become more unevenly distributed and the frequency of extreme events (extraordinary droughts, flash floods) will increase.\n\nEvery effort and environmentally conscious lifestyle that contributes to reducing greenhouse gas emissions and thereby to reducing the extent of climate change also contributes to protecting water bases and water resources.\n\nProtecting drinking water also requires appropriate information and conscious purchasing.\n\nFor example, you can use less water not only directly—through the tap—but indirectly as well: the production of new shoes and clothes—the cultivation of their raw materials, the making of the garments, dyeing—equally involves huge water demand and wastewater generation.\n\nTherefore, to complement your wardrobe do not buy only new clothes; swap clothes with your acquaintances, or obtain like-new items from second-hand stores as well.

FenntartK23=With a little attention while driving you can save a lot on fuel, which also reduces your vehicle’s carbon dioxide emissions. What are these aspects?
FenntartK23V01=You observe speed limits and choose speed according to road conditions—this is an important factor, because besides the accelerated mass, air resistance most strongly influences consumption.
FenntartK23V02=If you don’t need it, you remove the roof rack, because carrying it empty is not only unnecessary extra weight, but it also increases air resistance, which also results in extra consumption.
FenntartK23V03=You turn off unnecessary consumers—the A/C (often it’s enough to lower the window a bit) and engine cooling–cabin heating are responsible for most of the extra consumption.
FenntartK23V04=When driving a manual, you always shift on time—for most cars this is at 2500 rpm—you don’t rev and overwork the engine, thus you save more.
FenntartK23V05=You only travel with as much load as you absolutely need—the car is not a storage room; every kilogram carried unnecessarily increases consumption.
FenntartK23V06=You maintain the engine and use the appropriate motor oil—if necessary, you have your car inspected even between mandatory technical checks, because an old or faulty engine can be a great fuel waster.
FenntartK23V07=You think ahead before braking, because the subsequent acceleration consumes the most energy—you only step on the brake and stop if you must; for a foreseeable obstacle you slow down gently using engine braking.
FenntartK23V08=You try to handle every single daily task by car—since you drive economically, the more you’re on the road, the more you save.
FenntartK23V09=With route planning in advance you optimize your trip—before traveling you choose the shortest and least busy route, or you use a GPS that also tracks traffic.
FenntartK23V10=You use the highest possible gear—at higher speed this ensures the optimal engine speed—in lower gears the engine revs faster, which means more fuel consumed.
FenntartK23V11=In general, but especially if you drive long distances, you reduce your speed, whether on a motorway or a side road—this is one of the biggest ways to save.
FenntartK23V12=When stationary you don’t run the engine unnecessarily—if for any reason you have to wait in the car, you turn off the engine.
FenntartK23V13=You check tire pressure and inflate the tires according to the service book’s specifications—overinflated, but especially underinflated tires can lead to up to 6 percent extra consumption.
FenntartK23M=With smart solutions—not only while driving but in every area of life—reductions in everyday energy use and carbon emissions do not negatively affect quality of life; in fact, they can increase your comfort.\n\nThe goal is not to give something up, but rather—by eliminating truly unnecessary emissions—to reduce harm and environmental impact day by day.\n\nIf you do so, let it fill you with a good feeling that you are effectively contributing to making your life more sustainable in both environmental and economic terms.

FenntartK24=There are many places in the household where you can reduce electricity consumption. From the listed considerations, select those that apply here!
FenntartK24V01=You only start ironing when the clothes are completely dry—the wet surface cools the iron, and heating it back up requires a lot of energy. 
FenntartK24V02=You wash clothes at 40 degrees—you clean only very dirty clothes at higher temperatures.
FenntartK24V03=With a power meter you measure your appliances’ consumption—older ones can be larger electricity consumers—and you replace those with consumption strikingly higher than factory values with new, energy-efficient appliances.
FenntartK24V04=You switch off the dishwasher before drying begins, because that’s when consumption is the highest—right after the program finishes you open the door; in the hot steam the dishes dry by themselves.
FenntartK24V05=You fit the refrigerator without an air gap into its place in the kitchen or pantry, so it won’t use extra energy for cooling even if there is a radiator or stove right next to it.
FenntartK24V06=You choose every electrical and household appliance to the household’s needs—an oversized TV, a fridge of too large a volume, or a tumble dryer that’s not strictly necessary all come with additional electricity use.
FenntartK24V07=You spare the mobile phone battery by reducing the screen brightness, protecting it from excessive temperature fluctuations, closing unused apps, or switching to airplane mode.
FenntartK24V08=You don’t defrost frozen food in the microwave; instead, you take it out of the deep freezer in time and place it in the refrigerator, or just before use you allow time for full thawing at room temperature.
FenntartK24V09=With timer switches you specify when plugged-in devices receive power, and you use smart plugs in which you program the timing function and control it even by voice or with an app.
FenntartK24V10=You use a thick-walled pot for cooking, because this way you can turn off the stove minutes before the food is done—the pot retains enough heat to finish cooking the food.
FenntartK24V11=You leave switched-off devices in standby, since during this they use insignificantly little energy, and they respond instantly to being turned on, which is a much more energy-intensive process.
FenntartK24V12=You regularly remove the frost and ice layer formed on the wall of the deep freezer, because due to its insulating effect the appliance uses extra energy for cooling.
FenntartK24V13=You choose appliances classified in the most energy-saving class, even if they are more expensive—the greatest savings can be achieved with these—the difference pays off through lower energy demand.
FenntartK24M=You can start switching to an energy-saving lifestyle at any time, and you’ll feel its effect on the next month’s bills.\n\nMoreover, a more livable environment and preserving the Earth’s resources for our grandchildren are important even if paying the monthly utility bill does not cause you serious headaches.\n\nEven a single small change is significant, because over decades many small savings can amount to huge sums.\n\nAcquiring green thinking brings with it an even more environmentally conscious lifestyle, with which we do even more to reduce our ecological footprint.\n\nPart of this is that you do not leave your devices in standby mode, because they can consume up to 10 percent of the electricity corresponding to their normal operation (especially older devices), and the amortization (wear, depreciation) of components under power is also higher.\n\nYou do not place the refrigerator or freezer next to a radiator or dishwasher, stove, or in direct sunlight, because this way they must use more energy to achieve proper cooling.\n\nWhen placing or building in the fridge, you ensure sufficient space (an air gap) for proper airflow around the appliance.

FenntartK25=A lot of energy can be saved in the household. Some things cost nothing, but there are also larger investments that pay off over time. Choose the correct actions!
FenntartK25V01=You use the delayed start function on the washing machine and dishwasher, and postpone their start to nighttime hours, when electricity is cheapest.
FenntartK25V02=You cook in reasonable quantities, you don’t make unnecessarily large portions—for economical cooking you use an induction hob, which is the most energy-efficient way of preparing food.
FenntartK25V03=For visiting web content and watching videos you use a low-energy tablet, and you use the high-consumption desktop computer only for activities that require high performance.
FenntartK25V04=You use a robot vacuum cleaner, which is energy-efficient, it does both vacuuming and mopping, and it can be started even when no one is at home, so it doesn’t disturb the family.
FenntartK25V05=You make use of daylight—you raise the shutters, draw the curtains apart, and let sunlight flow into your home.
FenntartK25V06=Among refrigerators you choose one with a NoFrost function, which automatically defrosts the freezer, so you don’t have to defrost it regularly, and higher energy consumption due to icing is reduced.
FenntartK25V07=You occasionally dust your appliances, because dust deposited on ventilation gaps holds back heat generated during operation and therefore the appliance’s operating temperature and consumption increase.
FenntartK25V08=If you have a smart boiler, you set it so that for water heating it especially considers the periods when the price of electricity is the lowest.
FenntartK25V09=Instead of or alongside electric heating you install a stove or fireplace for heating—this, besides being decorative, also saves electricity, and you can use eco-friendly briquettes or pellets instead of coal.
FenntartK25V10=When you use an air conditioner in the home, you also ventilate with windows wide open—this refreshes the air faster and reaches the desired temperature sooner.
FenntartK25V11=Devices that work with water (e.g., washing machine, dishwasher, kettle) consume more in case of limescale deposits, so you regularly descale them with vinegar or other natural descalers.
FenntartK25V12=You have solar panels installed on your roof, complemented with a battery storage system—this compensates for consumption fluctuations and can even make energy independence achievable.
FenntartK25V13=The refrigerator is a major electricity user, so you supervise it—you check the door seal, place it further from heat sources (sunshine, heater, stove), don’t open it often, don’t put hot food into it, and keep its ventilation opening clear.
FenntartK25M=It is right and natural that while you want to maintain your comfort and standard of living, you also want to reduce your energy consumption.\n\nTherefore, use the possibilities of current technology as wisely as possible and do not waste it unnecessarily.\n\nThis will not only make your self-esteem higher, but also leave more in your wallet, and your life will become more sustainable.

FenntartK26=A great deal of energy can be saved in the household, but a great deal can also be wasted. Select the energy-moderate practices!
FenntartK26V01=Whenever possible, you travel by bicycle or on foot instead of by car—the car is a more costly, more energy-demanding device than any other used in the household.
FenntartK26V02=You do not cook at a full boil until the food is done; after reaching boiling point, you switch to a lower flame or a simmer.
FenntartK26V03=You do not leave any electrical device under power if you are not using it—every device plugged into a socket has electricity consumption.
FenntartK26V04=Instead of the elevator you take the stairs—the elevator is a transport device with high energy demand, and stair climbing is good for your health.
FenntartK26V05=If you are still before house design, you plan the house so that each room receives enough natural light from outside for its activities—thus you will need fewer lights during the day.
FenntartK26V06=In less-used rooms (e.g., pantry, basement, garage) you use motion-sensor lighting, so you never forget to switch it off.
FenntartK26V07=You always wash dishes by hand, because even hand-washing with running hot water is more energy- and water-efficient than a machine wash started fully loaded at a lower temperature.
FenntartK26V08=The tumble dryer works with a lot of energy—therefore you try to skip it by choosing a thorough spin program at the end of the wash so that clothes dry faster in the air.
FenntartK26V09=At home you also dress according to the season—in winter you wear a sweater and long trousers, in summer you dress casually.
FenntartK26V10=If you cannot do without a tumble dryer, then you choose the energy-saving heat pump version, and you only start it when it is fully loaded and you put dryer balls in it, which toss the clothes so they dry faster.
FenntartK26V11=You buy domestic products, because this way they do not have to be transported from far away to your country, to your favorite store—thus you indirectly contribute to reducing the energy demand tied to products.
FenntartK26V12=Limescale deposits and food and grease residues accumulating on the filter impair the dishwasher’s efficiency—therefore you maintain the appliance regularly with machine-cleaning additives and by manually cleaning the filter.
FenntartK26V13=You maintain your chosen temperature at home with a smart thermostat, which can dynamically regulate the temperature according to the family’s habits and schedule.
FenntartK26M=One of today’s greatest problems is unnecessary energy use—and one of its disadvantages is that our utility bills also increase significantly.\n\nA much more serious problem is that with excessive energy use we first induce global warming, and second we continuously pollute the air, which has a negative effect on the health of every single living being—be it plant, animal, or human.\n\nThe solution, however, is not complicated; everyone can do their part with smaller or larger, cost-free or possibly more expensive energy-saving tricks, and with their application and a little attention we can reduce environmental burdens a lot.

FenntartK27=People living in a sustainable home consciously reduce their ecological footprint. Select the relevant points!
FenntartK27V01=For renovating your home you use surface treatment materials and paints free of chemicals and environmentally friendly—with these you protect not only the environment but your own health as well.
FenntartK27V02=For furniture and coverings you choose natural materials from sustainable sources—wood, bamboo, or recycled materials.

FenntartK27V05=You switch to a plant-based diet—the production of meat and dairy products requires a large amount of natural resources, so if you reduce their consumption, you also significantly reduce your ecological footprint.
FenntartK27V06=You install solar panels on your roof—although this requires a larger initial investment, in the long run it reduces energy bills and provides a sustainable energy source.
FenntartK27V07=Instead of getting rid of old furniture or electronic devices, you try to repair them or find new uses for them.
FenntartK27V08=You use LED bulbs instead of traditional bulbs, which consume less energy and have a longer lifespan.
FenntartK27V09=For the house’s heating and cooling you use an intelligent thermostat—smart thermostats automatically regulate heating and cooling, thus helping to optimize energy use.
FenntartK27V10=You compost household green waste—this not only reduces the amount of waste but also produces valuable soil nutrients for the garden or houseplants.
FenntartK27V11=If you don’t have the financial means for your own solar panels, you choose a green energy provider—this is an energy supplier that provides energy from renewable sources.
FenntartK27V12=You improve your home’s insulation—proper insulation prevents heat loss in winter and the ingress of excessive heat in summer, thus reducing energy spent on heating and cooling.
FenntartK27V13=You buy local and seasonal products—this not only reduces the carbon dioxide emissions caused by transport (and transport also contributes to the spread of invasive species), but it also supports local producers.
FenntartK27M=Reducing your ecological footprint is one of the most important steps toward living more responsibly and contributing to the protection of our planet.\n\nWith small changes in your home, you can not only mitigate your impact on the environment, but also save energy and money.\n\nMake your home more sustainable, too!

FenntartK28=Let there be less trash in your environment! Which considerations involve less waste generation? Choose these!
FenntartK28V01=Instead of single-use sandwich packaging, aluminum foil, and snack bags, you use a Velcro fabric cloth, you bake pastries in a covered glass dish, or you cover the top with another baking tray, and to cover food in the fridge you use a small plate, a lid, or waxed cotton fabric.
FenntartK28V02=When diapering a baby, you use washable, many-times-reusable (possibly plant-based and free of harmful substances) diapers and soft flannel cloths; if wipes are still necessary, you make sure their quality and composition do not place a heavy burden on the environment.
FenntartK28V03=You don’t buy any items made of plastic or partly plastic for your household—neither electronic equipment nor other utility or comfort items or decorative objects—thus contributing to there being less plastic in your environment.
FenntartK28V04=You don’t accept promotional items, you use office supplies made of durable, natural, or recycled materials, you only print if necessary, and you reuse spoiled paper sheets that do not contain confidential data as drawing paper at home, or donate them to a kindergarten.
FenntartK28V05=You sort all your waste selectively, and you compost plant waste—as a result, a much smaller amount ends up in your municipal waste container, which you can switch to a smaller, cheaper bin.
FenntartK28V06=Paper has value, so you collect your printed newspapers, tie them up, and hand them in at selective or primary school paper drives—however, the best is to switch to electronic press.
FenntartK28V07=To remove makeup you use a cotton cloth that can be washed in the washing machine, which you moisten with water and, depending on the type of makeup, you add a little makeup remover cream or natural plant oil to wipe it off.
FenntartK28V08=In the store you take a good look at what you buy; you prepare for shopping with canvas bags, containers, and also with a shopping list to avoid overbuying—and in addition, you plan the weekly menu in advance, including breakfast and snacks.
FenntartK28V09=For shaving you use the tried-and-true all-metal safety razor instead of disposable plastic razors, with a pleasantly scented shaving soap.
FenntartK28V10=From synthetic-fiber clothes, microfibers are shed during washing, drying, and wearing, which pollute the water and the air—therefore you prefer natural materials, e.g., cotton, or even organic cotton, because its raw material comes from environmentally friendly farming.
FenntartK28V11=You use fewer types of skincare cosmetics with simpler compositions, free of unnecessary ingredients, and only in the necessary amount; you might even prepare them yourself and store them in glass containers—this is the best case.
FenntartK28V12=During menstruation you use environmentally friendly tools, for example a menstrual cup or washable pads, or eco pads free of harmful chemicals.
FenntartK28V13=You look into how your waste should be handled and how it can be handed in—what can go into selective collection, what can be taken to a waste yard, and which substances to avoid that are hazardous when entering soil or water.
FenntartK28M=To generate less trash and step onto the path of a more environmentally conscious lifestyle, you don’t necessarily need drastic changes—what matters is to move toward sustainability in small but continuous steps.\n\nThe feeling of a cleaner environment forming around you will fill you with good feelings, which will drive you further along this great path—and with this, while setting an example, you also spare Earth’s natural resources.\n\nCompletely replacing plastics is a “thing” that most modern households cannot achieve today—plastics cannot be completely avoided.\n\nWhy? Just look around your home: in the kitchen, the living room, the bathroom, the study, the car, or the attic... In recent decades, plastic has completely surrounded us.

FenntartK29=It is in our common interest to produce less waste, because then fewer harmful landfills would be needed and less waste would end up in the oceans. Select the activities that involve less waste generation!
FenntartK29V01=You store your food in lunch or meal boxes preferably made of metal or glass; moreover, if you eat at a canteen, you ask for the food in such a box—unlike plastic boxes, these boxes will serve you for many years.
FenntartK29V02=When brushing your teeth, you avoid products that, once worn out or emptied, become municipal waste—therefore you buy toothpaste and mouthwash in glass containers (e.g., Georganics), and you use a toothbrush made of natural material.
FenntartK29V03=You don’t buy pre-packaged staples (e.g., poppy seeds, walnuts, rice, flour, pasta, packaged vegetables and fruits), so you shop in zero-waste stores or have the goods dispensed into your glass containers or canvas bag.
FenntartK29V04=You collect all your waste and trash selectively; even the empty squeezable tube, the pizza box with food residue, the greasy chips bag, and the broken toy all have their place—because everything is taken and recycled.
FenntartK29V05=At the butcher’s and meat counter you ask for meats and cold cuts in your own clean containers instead of plastic bags and multilayer salami papers—the more of us request this, the more likely traders will respond and change will start.
FenntartK29V06=You bake bread or pastries for yourself, or you buy at a bakery where you ask for the products in a clean canvas bag; at self-service counters where baked goods must be visible, you use a many-times-usable, thin-threaded, densely woven, transparent textile bag.
FenntartK29V07=You avoid microplastics as much as possible—these are not only produced by the disintegration of plastics but are also contained in certain products—e.g., some body scrubs and toothpastes, as well as bottled water and polyester clothes.
FenntartK29V08=You try to buy milk and dairy products from a producer who also sells in your area, from whom you can get them in your own containers or in returnable glass containers—thus you free yourself from a lot of waste.
FenntartK29V09=You don’t buy products whose packaging isn’t even suitable for recycling—such as foam trays, foam boxes, and metallized plastic pouches.
FenntartK29V10=Instead of small, individually—often non-recyclably—wrapped chocolates, bonbons, muesli bars, and candies, you make homemade treats, or you buy sweets by weight, or choose those with recyclable packaging.
FenntartK29V11=You don’t use a plastic bag for weighing and buying vegetables, fruits, and baked goods; after weighing and paying, you put them straight into your basket; at supermarket self-service weighing counters you put produce into light, transparent, reusable little bags.
FenntartK29V12=Instead of paper tissues and kitchen paper towels you switch to cloth handkerchiefs, cloth napkins, and cotton rags—these (often dirtier than clothes) can be washed clean at higher temperatures (60 degrees), even together with towels, and can be used many times.
FenntartK29V13=You avoid single-use plastics—you use your own glass or metal bottle every day, you don’t need plastic bottles and cups, and you smoke less (if you do), because nearly one-third of ocean waste consists of cigarette butts—mostly plastic—that pollute the water.
FenntartK29M=There are countless landfills worldwide, consisting mostly of non-recyclable trash and plastic waste, and the seas and oceans also have to cope with a huge plastic burden.\n\nThe reason is that more waste is generated than can be processed, and among these there are many that cannot be processed at all—or there is no effort to recycle them.\n\nThe fate of such completely unnecessary waste is either incineration or release into nature.\n\nWhat can you do?\n\nIn addition to collecting your waste selectively, do everything to minimize the amount of plastic waste generated in your household—because the best waste is the waste that doesn’t arise.\n\nSo collecting selectively is indeed necessary, and washing contaminated plastic bottles isn’t pointless and (rinsed with used dishwater) not necessarily a waste of water, because only separated and clean waste has a chance to be recycled.\n\nHowever, care must be taken that recycling doesn’t turn into “wishcycling,” when the inclination to recycle is only apparent and shifts the problem to others (e.g., you throw dirty, food-contaminated, or non-recyclable plastic into the selective waste container with the thought that someone else will sort and wash the trash).

FenntartK30=During bathroom activities and in the case of products purchased for the bathroom, you can also do a lot for sustainability. Select the relevant activities!
FenntartK30V01=On product packaging you look for the logos and certifications that indicate sustainable production (e.g., FSC, EU Ecolabel).
FenntartK30V02=You pay attention to where the product you buy comes from and how far it travels to reach you—the closer it is, the more sustainable it is in terms of transport.
FenntartK30V03=You don’t buy single-use and/or plastic packaging—good packaging is made from recycled material or is fully recyclable.
FenntartK30V04=When showering you set the water as hot as you can just tolerate—this cleans your skin better and also helps you keep showers short.
FenntartK30V05=You check the ingredients of the cosmetic or cleansing product you want to buy and look up their effects on health and nature.
FenntartK30V06=You shop in zero-packaging (or zero-waste) stores, so you’re sure not to bring home unnecessary packaging.
FenntartK30V07=When buying a hygiene-related product, you consider three aspects: it should clean well, smell good, and have an appropriate price—waste managers and wastewater treatment plants are there to deal with the accompanying environmental problems.
FenntartK30V08=Instead of bathing you shower for max. 4-5 minutes (to time this practically, use an hourglass or a wind-up kitchen timer), and you use a water-saving shower head and a washbasin faucet fitted with an aerator.
FenntartK30V09=Instead of shampoos and shower gels in plastic packaging and not particularly sustainable in their ingredients, you use eco-friendly hair soap packaged in paper or metal in the shower.
FenntartK30V10=You have a separate radiator installed in the bathroom next to the towel warmer, which is necessary to ensure at least 28-30 degrees in the room when bathing, because in such warmth you won’t feel cold even when wet before drying off.
FenntartK30V11=At the sink, instead of liquid soap in a plastic bottle you use a pleasantly scented, paper-packaged artisanal soap with nourishing ingredients—and by buying it you also support small producers and local entrepreneurs.
FenntartK30V12=Your toothpaste comes in a glass jar instead of a tube, your toothbrush has a replaceable head and a handle made of natural material, and when brushing your teeth you use a cup instead of running water.
FenntartK30V13=Your manual shaving set is plastic-free, durable, made of strong metal, or you use an electric shaver.
FenntartK30M=For assessing the sustainability of products belonging to a sustainable bathroom, there are three main areas: the packaging, the product itself, and the ingredients.\n\nBesides these, of course there are other important aspects; for example, it matters how many times a product circles the planet before it reaches the place of use—the shorter the distance a product travels, the more sustainable it is.\n\nSo if you truly want a sustainable bathroom, you must pay attention to using as little hot water as possible, not overheating the room, minimizing the amount of waste generated, and how environmentally friendly the products you use are and what effects they have on your health.\n\nBecause don’t forget: you come into daily contact with hygiene and cleaning agents, and you can be sure this will have some long-term effect—positive or negative—on your health.

FenntartK31=You can do a lot for more sustainable dishwashing. Select these activities!
FenntartK31V01=You wash dishes with an eco-friendly, biodegradable detergent—these are just as effective (even when washing with cold water) as strong but environmentally hazardous agents.
FenntartK31V02=You don’t wash dishes under running water—you pour lukewarm water into the sink and wash in that—you start with the cleaner items and gradually move toward the dirtier ones.
FenntartK31V03=After washing dishes you wipe the water around the sink with a cloth kitchen towel instead of paper towels.
FenntartK31V04=The material of your sink tray is durable, acid- and alkali-resistant, not prone to scratching or denting, and recyclable (e.g., made of stainless steel, quartz sand, or Tectonite).
FenntartK31V05=Your hand cleaning and scrubbing tools used for dishwashing are made of natural materials (coconut fiber, hemp, or a brush with natural bristles).
FenntartK31V06=You soak truly dirty, burnt-on pans for a few hours or even overnight—for this you use the remaining used water from the previous wash, thus saving water and detergent.
FenntartK31V07=You only wash dishes when necessary—you only start washing truly dirty dishes and cutlery—a plate that ended up in the sink with a few crumbs only needs wiping off and can go into the cupboard.
FenntartK31V08=You carry out rinsing under running water, but you turn the water off immediately after each rinse.
FenntartK31V09=Your dish sponge is made of plastic and, since the selection is large, you can easily find one that matches your needs exactly.
FenntartK31V10=When using a dishwasher you make sure to start it only when fully loaded, on a short program, at a moderate temperature, and you fill it with eco-friendly detergent.
FenntartK31V11=Based on a homemade recipe you prepare your own eco dishwashing liquid, ensuring it consists of plant ingredients, is phosphate-free, and the bottle is refillable.
FenntartK31V12=To wash less often, you leave the dirty dishes in the sink and its surroundings (for up to a week) until they don’t hinder cooking.
FenntartK31V13=When washing vegetables or fruit you collect the used water, because it is still perfectly suitable for watering your houseplants, and with the dirtier water you flush the toilet.
FenntartK31M=Dishwashing is an indispensable part of the household—for it to be truly sustainable, you must consider not only electricity and water use, but also the accessories needed for dishwashing.\n\nHowever, besides your own decisions, retailers and manufacturers are also needed, so that with your everyday decisions and choices you have the opportunity to reduce your ecological footprint.\n\nEvery product has an ecological footprint—one key to sustainability is to reduce this as much as possible.\n\nAmong the countless products it’s often hard to find those that are truly sustainable—to this end, look at the labels, logos, and certifications on product packaging.\n\nOnly buy the product if its certifications confirm sustainability, that is, if the product demonstrably places a smaller burden on the environment than other products serving the same purpose.\n\nOne of the most commonly used—and fastest to wear out—dishwashing items is the plastic dish sponge, which ends up in the municipal trash after it’s worn out.\n\nHowever, it not only increases the amount of municipal waste, but is also hazardous waste, partly because they can harbor cultures consisting of even hundreds of different types of bacteria, and partly because they are often made of foamed polyurethane, petroleum, bleach, and sulfates using multiple chemicals (e.g., triclosan, which affects the hormonal system and has antibacterial and antifungal effects), which, under the effect of hot water and scrubbing, leach out and end up in water and then wastewater.\n\nAnd if you don’t rinse the plates and cutlery properly, you also introduce microplastics from the sponges into your body.\n\nDish sponges, however, can easily be replaced with tools made of natural materials, so look for these products!

FenntartK32=Shop in an environmentally conscious way! How can you be a conscious shopper? Select the points that fit here!
FenntartK32V01=You support sustainable brands and companies with your money—you research companies’ sustainability policies and practices and buy from those committed to environmental protection and social responsibility.
FenntartK32V02=You pay attention to packaging—you avoid overpackaged products and look for recyclable, reusable, or compostable, as well as minimalist packaging.
FenntartK32V03=You consider buying used products—you can often find used but still working products in good condition—thus you reduce the environmental burden associated with manufacturing new products.
FenntartK32V04=You look for recyclable, many-times-reusable products—such as canvas bags, or durable plastic, glass, and metal bottles: their features are long lifespan and multiple-use.
FenntartK32V05=You buy local products—thereby supporting local farmers and producers, and local foods and products travel shorter distances, thus reducing the environmental burden of transport.
FenntartK32V06=You plan your shopping—you prepare the shopping list in advance, containing only the products that are truly necessary—thus you avoid unnecessary impulse purchases and reduce food and material waste.
FenntartK32V07=You share your knowledge about environmentally conscious shopping—raising awareness in the community contributes to the spread of an eco-conscious lifestyle.
FenntartK32V08=You get informed about products—on product labels and descriptions you read sustainability information and look for environmental marks, ratings, and certifications.
FenntartK32V09=When buying products you primarily consider promotions and prices, thus saving more—where products come from and how they arrive is the store’s concern.
FenntartK32V10=Instead of exotic products you buy seasonal foods—products arriving in their own season are typically fresher, tastier, and richer in nutrients than those coming from far away.
