FenntartK59M=Waste management must not only solve current problems but also contribute to a sustainable future.\n\nSmart waste handling and recycling help conserve resources, protect the environment and support economic development, and they enable us to care responsibly for future generations.\n\nWith conscious consumption and waste reduction you make a positive impact on the environment and shrink our ecological footprint.\n\nThese practices support sustainability, but it’s important that they be known, accessible and feasible for everyone in daily life—which requires continuous and deliberate education and outreach.

FenntartK60=Consumers play a key role in supporting sustainable agriculture. Select the factors through which, as a consumer, you contribute to sustainable agriculture!
FenntartK60V01=Reducing food waste—by adopting more conscious eating habits you try to use food completely, taking expiry dates into account.
FenntartK60V02=Eco-friendly packaging and transport—you buy products that arrive with sustainable packaging and logistics, which reduces environmental impacts and helps preserve biodiversity.
FenntartK60V03=Food self-reliance—you try to grow your most essential daily foods yourself—vegetables, fruit, herbs or animal products—because buying less from stores does more for sustainability.
FenntartK60V04=Awareness and education—you study sustainable farming practices and the food industry so that, understanding environmental and social impacts better, you can make more conscious purchasing decisions.
FenntartK60V05=Advocacy and social activism—you support groups and organizations that pressure companies and governments through campaigns and petitions to advance sustainability in food and agriculture.
FenntartK60V06=Time is money—you do your shopping in the shortest possible time, so your priority is finding items quickly as you dash through the aisles, regardless of how or where they were produced.
FenntartK60V07=Sustainable production practices—you support farmers who respect the environment and biodiversity with eco-friendly methods (e.g., chemical-free growing, preserving natural habitats).
FenntartK60V08=Seasonal sourcing—you choose fresh foods grown in their own season and as locally as possible instead of far-flung exotic products.
FenntartK60V09=Supporting local producers—you buy local products at local markets from local farmers, which not only helps the local economy but also cuts long transport routes.
FenntartK60V10=Buying quality ingredients—you avoid highly processed, additive-heavy products and store-bought ready foods; instead you source quality ingredients and prepare them at home.
FenntartK60V11=Fair trade—you’re happy to choose Fair Trade-labelled products, knowing they emphasize giving (Global South) producers a fair return.
FenntartK60V12=Avoiding overconsumption—at home (and in your shop, if you run one) you avoid stockpiling excess food; you acquire only as much as can certainly be used or sold.
FenntartK60V13=Healthy foods—you prioritize buying organic products, because foods grown with minimal environmental impact and maintained ecological balance matter to you.
FenntartK60M=Consumers play a significant role in supporting sustainable agriculture, because their purchasing decisions directly affect farming practices and producers.\n\nConscious choices and education help make agriculture and the food industry more environmentally friendly and socially just—which effectively protects the planet’s and people’s well-being.

FenntartK61=Community gardening is a collective effort in which a local community works together on a plot to grow its own food. How can you organize it?
FenntartK61V01=Get to know the local community—you talk with people about who’s interested in a community garden, what the local food needs are and how much support they could offer to establish the garden.
FenntartK61V02=Take courses—you look for gardening courses where you can learn the basics of sustainable cultivation and practices like composting and ecological plant protection.
FenntartK61V03=Find a suitable site—you seek a place with good sunlight, appropriate size and easy access.
FenntartK61V04=Create a support group—working with people and sharing responsibilities aid success, so you select leaders and define areas of responsibility.
FenntartK61V05=Draft the garden plan—you decide which plants to grow, how plots will be divided and how the garden will be cared for.
FenntartK61V06=Acquire tools and resources—this includes gardening tools and procuring seeds and seedlings; it’s worth applying for grants or asking local businesses to support startup costs.
FenntartK61V07=Keep sustainability in view—you stay mindful of sustainability aspects such as water and energy savings and organize the operation as eco-friendly as possible.
FenntartK61V08=Create a horticultural plan—you define plant selections and planting times suited to local climate and soil, and you design an irrigation system.
FenntartK61V09=Invite everyone to a work day—you announce a community work day when people help set up and plant the garden; this builds connections and involves people in the project.
FenntartK61V10=Maintain the garden—you ensure ongoing care and maintenance; you hold regular meetings and work days so people can take part.
FenntartK61V11=Share the harvest—when crops ripen you share produce among community members and help with preparing the foods grown.
FenntartK61V12=Promote the benefits—you publicize the initiative that strengthens local development and health in the local paper, on bulletin boards and local online media, and you invite interested people to join.
FenntartK61V13=Share your knowledge—you organize community events to pass on your experience; you show how to create a sustainable garden so others can draw inspiration from green, hands-on cultivation.
FenntartK61M=Creating a community garden is an exciting, joyful venture that strengthens your community’s development through cooperation and increases local, healthy food production.\n\nThese gardens are spaces where people work together to grow plants and produce food while building community spirit and ecological awareness.\n\nStarting a community garden takes time, but its benefits to community and environment are highly valuable, playing a key role in advancing sustainability and building a healthier community.\n\nThere’s a close link between ecological farming and food security—both are crucial to a sustainable future.\n\nEcological farming uses methods that minimize environmental impacts and support healthy soil and plants.\n\nFood security means safe access to food and a healthy diet for everyone.

FenntartK62=A healthy lifestyle supports adopting and maintaining a sustainable lifestyle. Select the activities that help maintain your health!
FenntartK62V01=Healthy nutrition—your diet is healthy and varied, rich in vegetables, fruit, whole grains, lean proteins and healthy fats, and you reduce sweet, salty and processed foods.
FenntartK62V02=Adequate rest—sleep and rest play a key role in maintaining health, so you aim for 7–9 hours of sleep and build a regular daily rest/relaxation routine.
FenntartK62V03=Regular movement and exercise—exercise is essential to a healthy lifestyle, so you do at least 150 minutes of moderate or 75 minutes of vigorous activity per week.
FenntartK62V04=Settling into home-only living—you believe you can protect your health only by staying home, so you venture out as little as possible, handle errands online and have food delivered.
FenntartK62V05=Being informed—you learn how healthcare works and what services are available (e.g., which hospitals and clinics provide emergency care) and you research health questions and options online.
FenntartK62V06=Avoiding harmful habits—you avoid smoking and excessive alcohol, as these cause many health problems.
FenntartK62V07=Maximizing comfort—you primarily seek greater comfort, believing a car, a big house or branded clothing also benefit your health.
FenntartK62V08=Stress management—you learn to manage stress through methods like meditation, yoga, relaxation or hobbies.
FenntartK62V09=Preventive care—you see a doctor or health professional regularly for screenings and checkups; early detection and preventive care are important.
FenntartK62V10=Proactivity—if health issues arise you don’t let them worsen; at any symptom or concern you consult a professional as soon as possible.
FenntartK62V11=Social connections—relationships and social support matter for a healthy life, so you spend time with friends and family and seek communities that support healthy goals.
FenntartK62V12=Following medical advice—if you see a specialist you follow their recommendations and instructions and attend regular follow-ups.
FenntartK62V13=Self-fulfilment—you pursue activities and hobbies that bring joy and help you thrive; fulfilment and satisfaction support health.
FenntartK62M=Adopting and maintaining a healthier lifestyle is crucial for good physical and mental health and it supports your commitment to a more sustainable way of living.\n\nTo live healthier and longer, you need to act for yourself.\n\nBe active—the exercise improves stamina, lowers cardiovascular risk and helps control weight—and prefer a healthy plant-forward diet.\n\nA balanced lifestyle benefits not only you but also those around you and the environment: it supports coexistence and social bonds and helps reduce harmful environmental impacts.

FenntartK63=Transport is one of the largest greenhouse-gas-emitting sectors. Select the transport-related activities that reduce greenhouse-gas emissions!
FenntartK63V01=Timing your trips—you try to avoid rush hours when traffic jams are common and cars idle for long periods, which raises fuel use.
FenntartK63V02=Saving time—you always choose the fastest possible mode and believe less time spent traveling always means fewer emissions.
FenntartK63V03=Choosing the most sustainable options—whenever possible you walk or cycle; these modes cut greenhouse-gas emissions the most.
FenntartK63V04=Choosing a fuel-efficient car—if you use an internal-combustion car, you pick more efficient models, e.g., hybrids or plug-ins, which emit less.
FenntartK63V05=Driving efficiently—you avoid hard accelerations and braking, which raise fuel consumption and emissions.
FenntartK63V06=Seeking alternatives to flying—where possible you choose ground transport (e.g., trains or buses) instead of flights to reduce aviation emissions.
FenntartK63V07=Supporting electric mobility—where you can, you consider e-bikes, scooters, mopeds and cars.
FenntartK63V08=Regular maintenance—you keep your car well maintained and use appropriate, correctly inflated tires for conditions.
FenntartK63V09=Keeping your car in constant use—you try to use it several times every day to achieve a better average consumption and pay it off sooner.
FenntartK63V10=Organizing carpools—when you need your car you share rides; carpooling helps reduce the number of cars on the road.
FenntartK63V11=Avoiding all travel—you stay home and get others to travel on your behalf to meet your needs (e.g., shopping, errands).
FenntartK63V12=Using public transport—mass transit carries many passengers at once, making travel more efficient and sustainable.
FenntartK63V13=Getting informed—you learn local transport options and research eco-friendly alternatives—and you use them.
FenntartK63M=One of today’s biggest environmental challenges is greenhouse-gas emissions, a main driver of global warming and climate change.\n\nA major source is the transport sector, including cars, planes and ships.\n\nBut each of us—including you—can cut transport emissions.\n\nShifting travel habits and choosing more sustainable modes are key steps toward environmental protection.\n\nChoose more sustainable transport—the small steps add up to big change.

FenntartK64=Fighting plastic pollution is essential not only for the environment but also to protect our health. How can you contribute to this?
FenntartK64V01=Be a conscious consumer—you read product labels and avoid those containing harmful plastics (e.g., BPA), and you choose products from sustainable sources made ethically.
FenntartK64V02=Cut plastic use—you choose products with alternative packaging (e.g., glass, metal, biodegradable materials) because they’re more likely recyclable; you use reusable bags, bottles and food containers.
FenntartK64V03=Choose natural materials—whenever possible you pick products made from natural materials; cotton, bamboo and wood often have lower impacts.
FenntartK64V04=Support sustainable companies—you buy from firms committed to sustainability that actively reduce plastics in their products and packaging.
FenntartK64V05=Skip bottled drinks—bottled water and soft drinks may contain microplastics, and plastic bottles are energy-intensive across their lifecycle; many end up in landfills or nature.
FenntartK64V06=Purify your water—you use filters to cut microplastics in tap water; filters help remove harmful contaminants and improve drinking quality.
FenntartK64V07=Inform and raise awareness—you share knowledge with others about plastic pollution and how to fight it; public awareness is key to change.
FenntartK64V08=Support local recycling—you take part in local programs and make sure you sort and dispose of waste correctly.
FenntartK64V09=Hold plastics back—you keep all plastic waste (packaging and broken plastic items) at home (e.g., in the attic) to ensure it won’t pollute nature.
FenntartK64V10=Join cleanups—you join or organize shoreline and riverside cleanups to contribute directly to restoring the environment.
FenntartK64V11=Avoid clothes made partly or wholly from plastic fabrics (polyester), because washing and machine-drying shed microplastics into water and air.
FenntartK64V12=Change your lifestyle—you adopt ways of living that generate less waste, such as the zero-waste philosophy.
FenntartK64V13=Call for stricter rules—you contact local representatives and urge regulations to reduce plastic use and measures to curb plastic pollution.
FenntartK64M=Plastic pollution is a global problem affecting every continent, with health impacts felt worldwide.\n\nPlastics and microplastics know no borders—they accumulate and travel across oceans, move up the food chain and ride air currents to the most remote regions, including Antarctica and the highest peaks.\n\nFighting plastic pollution protects your health and helps safeguard our planet’s future.\n\nEvery small step counts, and together we can achieve significant change.

FenntartK65=Food safety is one of the most important factors for human health and well-being. How can you contribute to food safety and cutting food waste?
FenntartK65V01=You don’t buy or stock excessive amounts of food, because if they expire you risk wasting them.
FenntartK65V02=You try to grow the most necessary foods at home (vegetables, fruit, herbs, animal products) to help ensure food security for your household.
FenntartK65V03=You learn and apply preservation methods for purchased or home-grown foods.
FenntartK65V04=You learn to recognize spoiled, potentially toxic and unsafe foods, and you think through what to do next time to avoid them.
FenntartK65V05=You compost plant-based household scraps and return the valuable compost to the soil, since good soil quality is a key part of food security.
FenntartK65V06=You master good food-hygiene practices so you store, prepare and consume foods correctly.
FenntartK65V07=You aim to eat everything you cook; leftovers are frozen (if suitable) so you can eat them later.
FenntartK65V08=You often eat out so you don’t have to deal with food origin, quality or preparation—and leftover waste isn’t your problem.
FenntartK65V09=You never throw food away; you aim to prepare only as much as will certainly be eaten.
FenntartK65V10=You buy only as much perishable food as you can cook and eat soon, and you always check expiry dates.
FenntartK65V11=You buy quality food and avoid products with lots of additives, uncertain expiry dates or packaging with hygiene defects.
FenntartK65V12=You buy from producers who grow their products with sustainable, eco-friendly farming.
FenntartK65V13=You buy packaged foods only when the packaging suits proper storage and is fully recyclable.
FenntartK65M=Food safety is essential to preserving people’s health and well-being, yet it’s threatened by factors such as population growth, climate change, natural disasters and problems in food production and distribution.\n\nSo, as a conscious consumer, pay attention to food sources: minimize food waste, support sustainable agriculture and learn how to handle different foods well.\n\nAvoiding food waste isn’t just about saving energy and money; it also reduces the farmland, water, fertilizer and pesticides needed, cutting the environmental harms of food production.\n\nChoose and use food consciously—this supports food security, meets your nutritional needs and protects your environment.\n\nSafeguarding food safety and achieving a safer, more sustainable food supply serve both current and future generations, with cooperation and education as key factors.\n\nEveryone has a role: together we can contribute to a healthier, more sustainable future.

FenntartK66=Alongside running your home responsibly, shifting toward sustainability at work also matters. How can you, as an employee or leader, help your workplace operate more sustainably?
FenntartK66V01=Use green transport—to promote sustainable mobility you choose greener alternatives, e.g., public transport, cycling or electric cars.
FenntartK66V02=Cut energy use—you use LED lighting, an automatic temperature-control system, power down unused devices and switch off unnecessary lights.
FenntartK66V03=Use digital tools to reduce paper—you leverage online storage (cloud services), take digital notes and hold online meetings.
FenntartK66V04=Hold green meetings and events—where possible you choose online meetings to avoid travel, paper handouts and bottled mineral water.
FenntartK66V05=Support eco-friendly office solutions—you use recycled paper, green stationery, furniture made from sustainable materials and durable kitchen and dining accessories, and you place green plants indoors.
FenntartK66V06=Support remote work—when possible you enable flexible work (also one of the best retention measures) so people can avoid time- and energy-intensive commuting.
FenntartK66V07=Optimize digital content—emails and online documents are useful, but you avoid excessive use and storage that can overload servers and drive extra investments and energy use.
FenntartK66V08=Encourage selective waste sorting—separating paper, plastic, glass and compostables and handling e-waste correctly cuts municipal waste and helps protect the environment.
FenntartK66V09=Adopt sustainable supply chains—you run a green vehicle fleet and optimize routes, and you use suppliers that offer sustainable products and operate responsibly.
FenntartK66V10=Provide green training and set motivating green goals—you raise employees’ awareness so they make more sustainable decisions at work and at home.
FenntartK66V11=Use eco-conscious advertising—digital advertising is not only more economical but also greener, as it needs no paper materials or physical distribution.
FenntartK66V12=Support a sustainable workplace culture—you ensure commitment to sustainability shows up not just in daily decisions but also in strategic goals.
FenntartK66V13=Invest in green technologies—you track innovations and buy energy-efficient devices, install solar panels and implement solutions that optimize water use.
FenntartK66M=Pursuing sustainability matters not only at home but also at work.\n\nAs awareness of environmental impacts grows, companies and employees alike recognize that making operations more sustainable is essential for our planet’s future.\n\nMore and more firms see that environmental and social responsibility affects not only the planet but also business results.\n\nIntegrating sustainability into workplace operations improves reputation and brings concrete benefits such as cost savings, higher employee satisfaction and stronger customer relationships.\n\nBe a builder of a sustainable workplace culture!

FenntartK67=Avoid the “fast fashion” trap and switch to the “slow fashion” trend. How can you shop consciously and sustainably in fashion?
FenntartK67V01=You buy quality, durable clothes—you consider not only price but product quality; durable, well-made items last longer, so you replace them less often and generate less waste.
FenntartK67V02=You buy clothes made from sustainable materials—organic cotton, hemp, linen and recycled polyester are not only more environmentally friendly, but also tend to be more durable, so you create less waste in the long run.
FenntartK67V03=You follow the latest trends day by day—you never miss a seemingly good deal, and you quickly get rid of clothes that are only a few weeks or months old to make room for new ones.
FenntartK67V04=You see through big promotions and eye-catchingly cheap items—these often come with poor quality; because they’re so cheap, returning them may not be worth it, so they just take up space.
FenntartK67V05=You support ethical brands—those that use sustainable materials, follow fair-trade principles and ensure ethical working conditions are better for the environment and society.
FenntartK67V06=You drop off non-recyclable old clothes at collection points—more and more businesses and initiatives collect, recycle and revive textiles, helping cut textile waste.
FenntartK67V07=You buy second-hand—instead of new, you look for quality, almost-new pieces in thrift shops or online marketplaces, which greatly reduces environmental impact and yields unique finds.
FenntartK67V08=You avoid unnecessary packaging—since growing plastic waste is a major environmental problem, you buy from shops that ship with minimal packaging and care about recyclability.
FenntartK67V09=You make or alter clothes—you try to upcycle older garments; altering, dyeing or sewing are creative ways to extend their life.
FenntartK67V10=Your wardrobe is driven mainly by newness and low price—your priority is that clothes are new and as cheap as possible; you always buy many (and many types) at once, believing the more you buy, the more you save.
FenntartK67V11=You choose accurate sizing and styles that suit you—returns need shipping, cleaning and storage, which use energy and space; this isn’t always worth it for retailers and clothes can become waste.
FenntartK67V12=You curb overconsumption—online convenience and choice encourage frequent and/or unnecessary buying, but you purchase only what you truly need and avoid stockpiling clothing.
FenntartK67V13=You check where a garment comes from—the farther it travels, the greater the transport-related pollution; you buy as locally as possible to cut air and sea freight.
FenntartK67M=“Fast fashion” floods stores with cheap, trendy clothes that mirror rapidly changing styles and collections.\n\nRoutinely buying products that wear out quickly, become waste and are often made under polluting and unethical conditions harms both your wallet and the planet.\n\nProducing ever more low-cost, short-lived garments consumes huge amounts of water and energy, and chemicals used in textile manufacturing and plastic-based fibers cause serious environmental problems.\n\nConscious shopping helps you avoid the fast-fashion trap and support the more sustainable, ethical side of the industry.\n\n“Slow fashion” means seeking long-lasting, quality pieces that respect both the environment and society instead of chasing the newest trends.\n\nIt’s not about quick buys but deliberate choices that favor durable, sustainable clothing.

FenntartK68=The highest-footprint activities include meat consumption, transport, energy production, the fashion industry, poor waste management and construction. What can you do to operate more sustainably?
FenntartK68V01=Before pursuing a sustainable lifestyle, assess your footprint—ecological-footprint calculators offer practical tips to help you reduce it.
FenntartK68V02=Cut meat consumption, especially red meat—try plant-based alternatives, plant proteins and dairy substitutes, vegetables and fruit.
FenntartK68V03=Cycle and walk, support electric mobility, use public transport, seek alternatives to flying and use car-sharing services.
FenntartK68V04=Switch to renewable energy (e.g., solar, wind) and reduce energy use (e.g., energy-efficient devices, unplugging idle equipment).
FenntartK68V05=Buy fewer but higher-quality clothes—support sustainable fashion brands and choose recyclable, biodegradable, natural materials.
FenntartK68V06=Minimize waste—reduce plastic use, choose sustainable packaging solutions and prioritize recycling and composting.
FenntartK68V07=Leave sustainability questions and solutions to others—decision-makers, engineers and organizations—and keep living as before, adapting only if necessary.
FenntartK68V08=Support energy-saving, sustainable building practices—during construction and renovation choose eco-friendly building materials and natural options (e.g., wood, stone, recycled materials).
FenntartK68V09=Save water and energy—don’t hoard, cook only as much as you’ll eat and try to grow your essential foods.
FenntartK68V10=Choose long-life, sustainable products over cheap, disposable ones—items that are easy to reuse and recycle.
FenntartK68V11=Join community events that promote sustainability—tree plantings, community gardening or litter cleanups.
FenntartK68V12=Support sustainable economic and political initiatives by voting for leaders who back eco-friendly laws and regulations.
FenntartK68V13=Support local production and organic farms with your purchases—eat seasonal foods and use food-preservation methods.
FenntartK68M=The sectors with the largest ecological footprints include food production (especially meat), transport (notably car use and aviation), energy production/use (primarily burning fossil fuels—oil, gas and coal), the fashion industry (especially textiles and fast fashion), waste management (landfilling and lack of recycling) and construction (building and resource use).\n\nWe influence all of them through our purchases and daily actions—we can steer the systems that serve us toward greater efficiency and lower impact.\n\nBut this requires effort from all of us—a sustainable future is possible only if we consciously shrink our footprints.\n\nBy adopting a more sustainable lifestyle we can reduce resource overuse, curb climate change and help preserve biodiversity.\n\nIf everyone contributes to reducing their footprint, we can collectively preserve the planet and ensure a livable world for future generations.\n\nEcological-footprint calculators offer a quick, simple way to see your impact.\n\nPopular options include the Global Footprint Network calculator, WWF’s footprint calculator and the EPA (Environmental Protection Agency) calculators.\n\nCalculate your footprint and take steps toward a sustainable lifestyle based on the results!

FenntartK69=Building a conscious society is key to a sustainable future. Select the activities that help you become part of a society based on conscious decisions!
FenntartK69V01=Save energy—you use LED bulbs and energy-efficient appliances and unplug devices you’re not using.
FenntartK69V02=Reduce the waste you generate—you use reusable containers, compost, avoid over-packaged products and minimize single-use plastics.
FenntartK69V03=Buy local and seasonal foods—local products are fresher and tastier and have a smaller transport footprint, helping cut CO2 emissions.
FenntartK69V04=Save water—you use water-saving taps and shower heads, run water for less time and irrigate with collected rainwater.
FenntartK69V05=Reduce food waste—you plan what to buy and try to use ingredients you already have before buying new ones.
FenntartK69V06=Use eco-friendly transport—since transport is a major CO2 source, you choose public transit, cycling, walking or electric vehicles.
FenntartK69V07=Eat less meat—livestock production contributes significantly to climate change; by cutting meat and eating more plant-based foods you shrink your footprint.
FenntartK69V08=Watch ingredients—you read labels and choose products without harmful chemicals that won’t damage the environment.
FenntartK69V09=Buy from ethical brands—you support companies that operate transparently, use sustainable materials and back environmental initiatives.
FenntartK69V10=Join community programs—you take part in local green actions such as cleanups, tree plantings or community gardens.
FenntartK69V11=Focus on compliance—you believe different currents have always existed in society; if rules are enacted, you follow instructions and nothing more is needed.
FenntartK69V12=Learn about environmental protection—you read books, watch documentaries and inform yourself about how to live more sustainably.
FenntartK69V13=Share your knowledge—you talk with family, friends and colleagues about what you do for sustainability and encourage them to change too.
FenntartK69M=Climate change, pollution and overuse of resources pose serious threats to our planet.\n\nToday’s economic model emphasizes consumption and continuous growth, which is unsustainable in the long run.\n\nA conscious society instead prioritizes quality of life, reduced environmental burden and protection of natural resources.\n\nPeople consider not only their own interests but also those of the community and future generations.\n\nA conscious society is a community whose members actively strive for sustainable, ethical lifestyles.\n\nIt’s not only about knowing environmental problems but also acting to solve them.\n\nMembers take responsibility for their decisions—from consumption habits to energy use to which companies they support with their purchases.\n\nThe eco-friendly, sustainable lifestyle needed for this isn’t a trend; it’s a deliberate choice that helps preserve the planet for future generations.\n\nAnyone can begin, regardless of where they live or their finances—start with small steps that add up to significant impact.\n\nSustainable living not only protects the environment but also improves your quality of life.\n\nLess waste, lower bills, healthier eating and less stress—these are just a few benefits of living more consciously.\n\nRemember, every small change counts, and when many people act together, it makes a huge difference.\n\nStart today and help build a more sustainable future!

FenntartK70=Composting is a recycling process—the best, most natural thing that can happen to your household’s organic waste. Select the steps that belong to composting!
FenntartK70V01=Talk to your neighbors—you explain why you compost (and may even convince them of the benefits) and reassure them that a properly maintained composter won’t smell or attract pests.
FenntartK70V02=Decide what kind of composter you want—you set up a compost heap (the most nature-friendly method) or a compost bin, or buy a wooden, plastic or metal composter.
FenntartK70V03=Place the composter—the best spot is semi-shaded, accessible from all sides, on permeable soil, e.g., under a larger tree, so it doesn’t get too much direct sun and won’t be washed out by rain.
FenntartK70V04=Get the tools—for chopping waste to size use pruning shears, a small saw or hatchet; for turning the pile use a pitchfork or shovel; for screening finished humus use a sieve.
FenntartK70V05=Learn what can go in—generally, mix about 75% green waste (vegetables, fruit, grass) with 25% brown waste (twigs, wood chips, mulch).
FenntartK70V06=Learn what cannot go in—above all, nothing hazardous, just as in your municipal bin (e.g., kitchen fats, chemicals, medicines, spoiled food and cooked foods in general).
FenntartK70V07=Check kitchen scraps before adding—don’t let them sit long in the caddy, mix them in quickly; if they’ve dried out, water them, and if too wet, add dry plant matter.
FenntartK70V08=Wash plant residues thoroughly before composting—ideally when produced in the kitchen, but at latest before adding; dirt and grime on them can spoil the compost.
FenntartK70V09=Keep adding kitchen plant waste—while maintaining correct ratios, mix in structure-loosening bulking agents (e.g., twigs, wood chips) to boost aeration.
FenntartK70V10=Occasionally add pieces of baked goods, bones, leftover meat and other cooked scraps, used cooking oil and a little candy—these accelerate composting and improve texture.
FenntartK70V11=Turn your compost every 4–6 weeks—check that the process is working, moisture is adequate, heat is building and there’s no rotting or mold; if there is, loosen the structure and mix, move the pile.
FenntartK70V12=Wait for the compost to mature—compost takes 3–12 months; at 3 months it may still contain substances harmful to sensitive plants.
FenntartK70V13=Use the finished compost—it improves soil for trees, shrubs and vegetable beds and provides excellent nutrients for balcony planters and houseplants.
FenntartK70M=Composting significantly reduces your household’s waste volume.\n\nValuable organic (plant) waste doesn’t end up in the bin but returns to nature’s organic cycle.\n\nThis waste therefore doesn’t go to already overloaded landfills and isn’t incinerated.\n\nCompared with burning, composting produces far less CO2—more carbon returns to the soil and less to the air—so composting helps cut air pollution and greenhouse gases.\n\nDuring composting, organic matter oxidizes and decomposes, producing carbon dioxide, minerals and humus.\n\nWell-maintained compost improves the quality of garden and vegetable-bed soils and provides excellent nutrients for terrace or indoor houseplants.\n\nIf you live in a city without a garden but want to compost, join a community-composting initiative.\n\nEntire buildings or neighborhoods can work together to recycle their organic waste—and use the finished humus to improve soil in balcony boxes and indoor pots.

FenntartK71=Environmental awareness is no longer just a virtue but an expectation. Select the activities through which you can actively contribute to sustainable living!
FenntartK71V01=Cut meat and cheese consumption—beyond industrial animal farming being deemed a global health hazard, it consumes huge amounts of energy and water and requires vast cropland and pasture.
FenntartK71V02=Plant trees regularly, but only if you can care for them—tree planting is among the noblest things you can do for wildlife and to reduce climate-change impacts.
FenntartK71V03=Sort your waste—waste is a resource and excellent secondary raw material: metal, paper, plastic and glass can get a second life when recycled.
FenntartK71V04=Buy local and seasonal—this supports the domestic economy and curbs climate-warming emissions from long-distance transport.
FenntartK71V05=Protect animals and wildlife—litter alone endangers wildlife, but cruelty and abandonment exist too, so report animal abuse, adopt from shelters and take injured animals to a veterinary hospital.
FenntartK71V06=Avoid waste and overconsumption—don’t buy unnecessarily; get only what you truly need—and that applies not only to food but also to drinking water and electricity.
FenntartK71V07=Switch to vegetarian or vegan living—this greatly helps shrink your footprint and protect the environment.
FenntartK71V08=Never burn household waste and compost what you can—kitchen and garden green waste is most easily eliminated and recycled on site by composting.
FenntartK71V09=Don’t litter—wherever you go, never drop trash; use public bins or, if there aren’t any, take it home; never dump waste in nature.
FenntartK71V10=Garden consciously and practice self-reliance—it’s a unique way to unwind by reconnecting with nature, it saves money and yields healthy, tasty food.
FenntartK71V11=Shop without waste—you go to farmers’ markets, avoid over-packaged products and use cloth bags and baskets for produce.
FenntartK71V12=Promote eco-living and environmental protection—you organize green events, encourage others to live sustainably and become a green influencer who inspires people.
FenntartK71V13=Prioritize mere compliance—you focus only on meeting your own needs and requirements, simply following climate-driven changes that shops and service providers make.
FenntartK71M=Environmental awareness is a complex concept embracing consciousness, sensitivity and responsibility toward the environment.\n\nIt has become increasingly important due to the shocking effects of climate change and the spread of sustainable development and healthy lifestyles.\n\nAn eco-conscious person understands environmental problems and strives to live in ways that minimize harm to Earth.\n\nIt may seem difficult at first, but often it costs almost nothing.\n\nMain steps include awareness (learn about issues like climate change, air pollution and biodiversity loss and their causes and consequences), sensitivity (pay attention to your surroundings, notice changes, care about Earth’s future), responsibility (commit to sustainability and aim not to burden the environment) and action (actively protect the environment, change your lifestyle and support green initiatives).

FenntartK72=Coffee isn’t exactly eco-friendly due to its large climate footprint, but if you do drink it, recognize that coffee grounds—its by-product—are highly versatile. Select their uses!
FenntartK72V01=Neutralizing odors—it deodorizes fridges (place a small dish inside), can be put in shoes, bags and gym clothes, neutralizes tobacco smoke and, in water, removes unpleasant smells from cookware.
FenntartK72V02=Cat-toilet deterrent—its compounds repel cats, helping keep cat feces out of the garden.
FenntartK72V03=Repelling mosquitoes and other insects—placed in a diffuser, the caffeine and other compounds repel mosquitoes and other bugs.
FenntartK72V04=Reducing pet odor and removing fleas—after bathing the animal, rub in coffee grounds and then rinse off (external use only; do not let animals ingest, as it may be harmful).
FenntartK72V05=Enriching garden and seedling soil—you can scatter grounds on the lawn; grounds-enriched potting mix is an excellent base for raising seedlings at the start of the season (start collecting grounds earlier and store airtight to prevent mold).
FenntartK72V06=Reducing musty indoor smells and cleaning fireplaces—placed in a musty room it reduces odor; sprinkled on ash it reduces color, smell and ash clouds.
FenntartK72V07=DIY cosmetics and natural dye—combined with natural ingredients, caffeine can serve as a body scrub, hair thickener, hair-growth booster and anti-cellulite aid, and it can dye cotton, rayon and paper or stain and color wooden objects.
FenntartK72V08=Improving houseplant soil—rich in nitrogen, potassium, magnesium and phosphorus, grounds can be mixed into soil or dissolved in water and applied by watering (acid-loving plants especially like it).
FenntartK72V09=Multiple re-brewing—grounds can be placed back into the coffee maker and brewed several times without losing flavor or aroma.
FenntartK72V10=Abrasive and antibacterial cleaner—its fine, gritty particles make it a scrub for dry kitchen surfaces (e.g., stovetops, grills) and, with water, it can help maintain sink drains and pipes.
FenntartK72V11=Mushroom growing—it makes soil mineral-rich, slightly acidic and mildly sour, which favors mushrooms that won’t (or rarely) grow in typical garden soil.
FenntartK72V12=Compost—one of the best ways to recycle plant-based grounds; it boosts compost nutrients, helps generate and retain heat and contributes to moisture retention.
FenntartK72V13=Slug and ant deterrent—it keeps slugs and snails away from plants; scattered among vulnerable plants and flowers, its odor masks them from ants.
FenntartK72M=Coffee is widespread worldwide thanks to its positive effects on people: caffeine is stimulating, can aid digestion and supports vascular function.\n\nBut coffee also has downsides—overconsumption, production and the waste it creates carry major environmental impacts.\n\nCoffee growing demands care, labor, chemical treatments, lots of water (about 140 liters per cup) and vast farmland.\n\nSo try to reduce your coffee consumption (if you drink it), and treat valuable grounds not as waste but as a versatile resource!

FenntartK73=Composting reduces the organic waste that accumulates in the environment, and its end product—compost—improves soil fertility. Select the ingredients that can go into compost!
FenntartK73V01=Residues of un-sprayed, seasonal fruits and vegetables—cores, peels, leaves, spoiled produce.
FenntartK73V02=Coffee grounds, ground coffee.
FenntartK73V03=Crushed eggshells, small amounts of wood ash.
FenntartK73V04=Manure from herbivores (hamsters, poultry, rabbits, horses, cows, goats).
FenntartK73V05=Chemical-free (unpainted, uncoated) wood shavings and sawdust.
FenntartK73V06=Cut, clean paper without lacquered or painted surfaces.
FenntartK73V07=Disease-free garden green waste (mown grass, leaves, chopped twigs; except walnut leaves and needles of oily evergreens).
FenntartK73V08=Plastic-free tea bags, loose tea, culinary and medicinal herbs.
FenntartK73V09=Prepared foods (meat, dairy, baked goods), animal fats, bones, cooked leftovers, feces of carnivorous pets (dogs, cats) and humans, cat litter, swept dust, sand, coal ash.
FenntartK73V10=Weeds before flowering, or weeds without flowers.
FenntartK73V11=Inorganic materials (plastic, metal, aluminum, glass), latex (balloons, gloves), paraffin (candles, wax paper), bioplastics, sewage, used oil, hygiene products (e.g., diapers, wipes).
FenntartK73V12=Dead parts of houseplants, spent potting soil.
FenntartK73V13=Larger branches, trunks, flowering weeds, resinous/oily plants (e.g.,  conifers), walnut leaves, chemically treated plants (e.g., peels of non-organic tropical fruit).
FenntartK73M=Composting is essentially the decomposition of organic waste—organic materials from the garden and household rot in the presence of oxygen and turn into humus.\n\nMicroorganisms and other life forms (fungi, worms, earthworms, snails) participate in the process.\n\nThe end product is a nutrient-rich organic resource that functions as a natural fertilizer in the garden.\n\nCompost is not for making all household waste disappear.\n\nIn general, inorganic materials, chemically treated plants and meats are forbidden, and the following must also be excluded:\n- chemically treated cardboard, painted/varnished paper (e.g., , magazines, catalogs, flyers, newspapers, food packaging, business cards—collect these separately for recycling);\n- sewage (may contain household chemicals);\n- used oil (can ruin the compost and slow decomposition);\n- hygiene products (strictly forbidden due to health risks);\n- cat litter, feces of carnivorous pets and humans (may contain pathogens and parasites—can be composted only with special care in separate systems);\n- coal ash (contains tar);\n- diseased or infected plants (can contaminate and ruin the compost);\n- inorganic items (plastic, metal, aluminum, glass—collect separately if recyclable);\n- latex (natural latex may decompose, but products often contain non-degradable synthetic additives);\n- paraffin (animal- or plant-based waxes like beeswax/soy wax are acceptable; paraffin wax from candles/wax paper is not, as it’s a fossil-fuel by-product);\n- bioplastics (made from plant or other renewable biomass but decompose effectively only in industrial systems);\n- larger branches, trunks (decompose very slowly and hinder turning);\n- flowering weeds (may spread in the garden);\n- chemically treated produce (contaminates the compost and later the soil);\n- animal fats, meat, bones and cooked kitchen leftovers (decompose slowly, smell, attract pests and wildlife that can dig it up);\n- resinous/oily plants (can spoil pH—compost separately; conifers can take up to 7 years);\n- walnut leaves and other oily plants (decompose very slowly and worsen pH—can be collected and composted separately).\n\nSlow-to-decompose leaves: walnut, chestnut, plane, oak, beech, poplar.\nFast-decomposing leaves: willow, hazel, ash, maple, alder, elm, birch and linden (these can be added in larger amounts).

FenntartK74=Selective waste collection is essential for environmental protection and moving toward a circular economy, but you can’t put everything in the sorting bins. Select the materials that can be collected selectively!

FenntartK74V05=Food scraps, used oil, cooking fat, kitchen and garden green waste, bulky waste (e.g., furniture, mattresses, carpets, suitcases), shoes, clothes.
FenntartK74V06=Household or cosmetic product bottles, clean plastic film, plastic bags and sacks.
FenntartK74V07=Oily, greasy, food-soiled paper or boxes (e.g., margarine tubs, greasy pizza boxes, deli wrappers).
FenntartK74V08=Cutlery, tin cans, beverage cans.
FenntartK74V09=Clear glass without caps (jars, mineral-water bottles, spirits bottles).
FenntartK74V10=Rinsed milk, sour-cream and yogurt cups.
FenntartK74V11=Plastic toys, hygiene waste (e.g tampons, diapers, toothbrushes, tissues, wipes), foil with metal inner layer (e.g., chip bags, chocolate wrappers).
FenntartK74V12=Colored glass without caps (wine and beer bottles).
FenntartK74V13=Aluminum foil, metal screw caps.
FenntartK74M=The possibility of recycling—and paving the way to it—is in your hands.\n\nWhen you start sorting waste at home, items that would otherwise go in the trash get a chance at a “second life.”\n\nSelective collection enables recycling, ensuring that the raw materials and energy used to make items don’t go to waste.\n\nRecycling requires less energy than extracting, transporting and processing virgin materials for new products.\n\nRecycling also reduces soil and air pollution by keeping waste out of landfills.\n\nWhat’s more, decomposing trash emits greenhouse gases (e.g., methane) that contribute to global warming.\n\nCollection containers are color-coded and labeled to show what goes inside.\n\nMake sure you put waste in clean and in the correct bin.\n\nSome items never belong in any sorting bin.\n\nBeyond the non-recyclables listed in this question, the following also must not go into selective bins: nylon stockings, CDs, audio/video cassettes, plastic cladding, fluorescent tubes, lightbulbs, window glass, mirrors, eyeglasses, porcelain, ceramics, heat-resistant glass, medicine bottles, blister packs, Styrofoam, electrical devices, e-waste, car tires, carbon paper, fax paper, receipts, dry-cell batteries, accumulators, cables, liquid hazardous waste (paint, glue, varnish).\n\nMany of these are usually accepted at municipal drop-off sites (e.g., bulky waste, tires, batteries, paint, bulbs, Styrofoam, electrical devices)—check in advance.\n\nCompost kitchen and garden green waste, and take used cooking oil/fat to designated collection points.\n\nAmong plastics, codes 1, 2, 4 and 5 are generally recyclable; codes 3, 6 and 7 usually are not and should go to municipal facilities.\n\nIf something can only be disposed of as general waste, consider how to avoid it next time.\n\nMost importantly, try to produce less waste—the best waste is what never exists!

FenntartK75M=Over a lifetime, a person generates about 600 times their body weight in waste—that’s truckloads.\n\nBurning trash in incinerators has a large carbon footprint, releasing significant greenhouse gases.\n\nYet much of what we accumulate can be recycled as secondary raw materials, a good way to cut air pollution, environmental burden and the exploitation of Earth—while sparing primary resources (e.g., wood, minerals).\n\nBetter than collecting and processing waste is preventing it in the first place—this not only helps the planet but also saves you money and time.

FenntartK76M=Eco-conscious living aims to shrink the footprint we generate day to day.\n\nIt’s a set of habits and behaviors that support environmental sustainability.\n\nCommon threads are reducing energy use and waste.\n\nTravel is unavoidable—whether to the store, school, work or a well-earned vacation.\n\nBut there are many ways to lessen its harms—before leaving home, choose the mode that fits the trip with the smallest footprint and consider offsetting your emissions.

FenntartK77=We must reshape consumption to make it more sustainable. Select the activities you can do at home to reduce pollution and waste!

FenntartK77M=Sustainable shopping and consumption aren’t just about using less plastic or choosing eco-friendly products.\n\nThey’re a conscious decision-making process that accounts for environmental impacts, social responsibility and economical use.\n\nSustainable consumption isn’t a trend but a necessary step to protect our planet.\n\nWith thoughtful choices you can reduce environmental burdens, support local economies and contribute to a more sustainable future.\n\nMost importantly, by changing shopping habits you can help the planet function better.

FenntartK81=The linear economy’s wasteful “use and toss” mindset must shift to the sustainable model of a circular economy for a livable future. How can you contribute?
