HatasLeirasMagyarazatSzoveg=The descriptions of environmental and natural impacts (as well as the more than 300 quiz questions and nearly 100 sustainability-related questions in the game) form a highlighted part of [z]The True Treasure[-] game.\n\nOur Earth struggles with [p]many very serious problems,[-] and the purpose of these descriptions—and of featuring environmental and natural problems in the game—is [z]to help you understand why these problems exist, how they developed,[-] and [z]what you yourself can do[-] to mitigate or avert them, and to restore and prevent the damage they cause.\n\nLet these descriptions not instill doubt in you; on the contrary, let them [z]strengthen your resolve to stand up against the various environmental problems![-]\n\n|&K36&[k]Let them prompt decisive action![-]|\n\nThere are more and more people, groups, and organizations [z]who do everything for a livable future.[-]\n\n|&K36&[k]Join them![-]|\n\n[z]Choose[-] one (or more) environmental problem and [z]be active in the environmental protection activities related to it![-] Of course, to do this, you must first thoroughly look into the issues you choose. Allow me [z]to offer you[-] the first steps with the impact descriptions.\n\nThe images in the impact descriptions come from the excellent image-sharing site Pixabay.com. It’s wonderful to see [z]how many artists are concerned about the fate of the Earth[-]—their stunning images and illustrations fit the descriptions of the problems perfectly.\n\nThe natural disasters and environmental impacts shown in the images [z]capture the moment when the pictures were taken.[-] This means that thanks to nature’s regenerative power and human restoration activities, some of the depicted problems may have been remedied by now—[z]if only that were true for all of them![-] But since we hear about new—and increasingly numerous—similar problems day by day, and we can encounter them in our own environment and experience them firsthand, the images—free of recognizable people, company and brand names, and logos—[z]depict the various impacts in a general way.[-]\n\nThe descriptions do not condemn any single country, nor hold any company or individual responsible; and for the images, it doesn’t matter when and where they were taken—this is about humanity, all of us—[p]we are equally responsible[-] for the environmental problems we cause.\n\nThe depictions and descriptions refer to numerous initiatives, movements, enterprises, and individuals [z]who speak out and act in exemplary ways for environmental protection,[-] and [z]who express concern and warn[-] against continuing environmental damage.\n\nThese descriptions were already relevant 30 years ago and will remain so 30 years from now, since globally [p]we are unlikely to give up fossil fuels by 2050;[-] we must also expect continued growth of the human population [p]for decades;[-] and truly environmentally conscious corporate and individual behavior is [p]only very slowly making headway.[-]\n\nTherefore, environmental impacts unfortunately [p]will not become obsolete[-] in the coming decades; indeed, they may even strengthen further.\n\nHowever, we are also in the midst of a process in which [z]we already know everything about environmental problems[-] and [z]we have tools to mitigate and prevent them.[-]\n\n[z]We should use this knowledge[-] and these tools now—the passage of time will judge whether we truly did everything.\n\n|&K36&[k]Why was The True Treasure project created?[-]|\n\nFirstly, because [z]our children must understand that they cannot carry on[-] [p]the ingrained, environment-damaging habits of previous generations;[-] secondly, [z]to draw attention to the endless daily struggles[-] of hundreds of millions of people against environmental impacts; thirdly, [z]to nudge people[-] out of the closed loop of their everyday routines and [z]direct their gaze to the vulnerable natural world;[-] and fourthly, [z]to encourage[-] developers and event organizers in the digital and real worlds that [z]many more projects and events are needed to promote environmental protection and sustainable living.[-]\n\nEvery word of the descriptions, every sentence, [z]serves the path toward our sustainable, shared future.[-]\n\nMy special thanks [z]to the credible environmental organizations[-] I contacted, [z]who made available the articles and news[-] on their portals to prepare the textual abstracts of the impact descriptions, thereby lending [z]credibility to the project.[-]\n\n[z]From them and from their dedication,[-] the project draws and conveys the message that for no interest whatsoever may we destroy [z]nature—our only ally[-] in the fight against climate change and our internal strife—instead [z]we must learn to live with it,[-] because we are part of it too.\n\n|&K36&[k]Therefore, the descriptions do not take our financial interests or comfort as their basis, but how we should live together with nature so that Earth remains livable for us and for all other living beings as long as possible.[-]|\n\nWhere we are headed is articulated clearly and firmly by two quotes from the world-famous naturalist, Sir David Attenborough:\n\n|&K30&[a]“It’s almost inconceivable that while we live our lives, the planet’s other creatures are experiencing a level of destruction akin to what once could be caused by the explosion of a colossal asteroid. Once our survival depended on nature—now nature’s survival depends on us. I’ve always been sure that people cannot protect nature until they get to know it and love it. Nature isn’t simply nice to have—it is vital to the existence of every single human being.”[-]|\n|&K30&[a]“We wiped out the predators, we can order food, we don’t need to fear epidemics. Nothing can stop us. Except ourselves.”[-]|\n|&K36&[k]20??[-]|\n\n[k]20??—What does this mean?[-]\n\nTaking into account the climate goals set at the UN COP international climate conferences and the continuously high greenhouse gas emission intensity resulting from the global use of fossil fuels, [p]we are heading toward not being able to keep warming within the 1.5 degrees Celsius threshold considered safe.[-]\n\nIf we exceed this notable value but, [z]through consistently environmentally conscious attitudes[-] at both state and individual levels everywhere in the world, we still manage to cool the planet back to a safe temperature, then the year of that notable moment will replace the question marks.\n\n[k]Postscript:[-]\n\nMany people, when they look at the multitude of cars inching along the road and the nearly empty train passing by, feel they can do nothing on their own against global environmental problems—which, moreover, no one likes to read about, mention, or even acknowledge.\n\nIt’s undeniable that decision-makers and companies have more tools to tip the process toward sustainability and to persuade people to change their lifestyles; however, [z]individual environmentally conscious actions are also of inestimable value:[-] they bring problems to the surface, thereby also urging solutions—and well-thought-out eco-conscious actions inspire others and set an example for them.\n\nThere are three actions with which we can fight climate change most effectively—even individually: one is [z]avoiding overconsumption and waste,[-] the second is [z]reducing meat consumption,[-] and the third is [z]moving toward self-sufficiency.[-]\n\nBefore you declare that you don’t waste, think through how many times you fuel the car (or your family members do) in a month; how many times you fly in a year; how much municipal and recyclable waste you generate weekly; how much prepared yet uneaten food you throw away daily; how much electricity you use and how much wastewater you produce monthly; how well insulated your home is and whether you use renewable energy sources.\n\nYou can maintain your standard of living while [z]practicing moderation in your consumption through mindful purchases and choosing durable, quality products and services that create little waste[-]—this benefits the planet and thus the next generations as well.\n\n[z]Reducing meat consumption and switching to a plant-based diet also greatly reduces environmental impacts:[-] besides effectively supporting your health with this change, it would help us shift away from predominantly industrial-scale, animal-feed-focused cultivation toward food production for humans that requires less land and treats soil and the environment more gently—easing the food crisis as well.\n\nThe vast land need for grazing and feed production would decrease (the freed areas, once restored, could be returned to nature as protected areas); deforestation and forest burning stemming from these would decrease; greenhouse gas emissions and environmental harm from transport, from livestock in industrial animal husbandry, from machinery, and from monoculture agriculture’s fertilizer- and pesticide-based soil practices would decrease—and not least, we would save the lives of many animals, indeed they would not even have to be born.\n\n[z]Self-sufficiency is among the most environmentally friendly activities.[-]\n\nProduce your staple foods yourself: grow vegetables and fruits, and keep some livestock to meet your needs for meat, milk, and eggs.\n\nIf you cannot do this, you still support self-sufficiency (and a healthy lifestyle) by sourcing your food needs from local markets, local producers, and organic farms who often produce seasonal, often organic-certified goods using optimal, sparing use of drinking water and gentle use of arable land, and who raise their animals in free-range, ethical conditions.\n\nSelf-sufficiency naturally reduces waste, involves little refuse and pollution, is efficient in tilling the land and using water, and makes the self-sufficient person as independent as possible from supermarkets, industrial farms, and prices.\n\n|&K36&[k]What can we do?[-]|\n\n[z]Carry out as many activities as possible that keep the safety and health of our environment in mind,[-] because this increases the chance that others will understand why we do it and will follow us.\n\n[z]This behavior will ensure the path toward the kind of future we all envision for ourselves.[-]\n\n|&K36&[k]Be an example yourself![-]|\n
FenntarthatobbEletSzoveg=|&K45&[z]Striving for a more sustainable life[-]|\n[p]We face severe sustainability problems:[-] in just under seven months humanity consumes as many resources as would be available for an entire year if we respected the planet’s renewal capacity (in 2025, Earth Overshoot Day fell on July 24).\n\nWe are extremely wasteful with land, water, and energy; we generate a lot of waste and garbage; we pollute the soil, the water, and the air.\n\n[p]With such high levels of waste, overconsumption, and pollution, Earth’s resource reserves will be exhausted.[-]\n\nSince agriculture and industry directly or indirectly serve households and individual consumers, [z]we can facilitate their transformation toward sustainability by changing our consumption habits and needs—through which we ourselves become more sustainable.[-]\n\n|&K36&[k]What can you do for a more sustainable life?[-]|\n\nThere are no short, quick answers, because we all do different activities, have different jobs, and live our lives differently.\n\nA more sustainable life is compatible neither in the short nor in the long term with pollution, the destruction of nature, and climate change; therefore we need measures that effectively mitigate these.\n\nThere are groups of activities and their actions that, from a sustainability perspective, stand out from the rest—[z]by considering these you can take a big step toward an eco-conscious lifestyle.[-]\n\nYou don’t have to (and cannot) adopt every measure at once, [z]but strive to add a new tip to your life every week or month.[-]\n\nThe list is not necessarily a ranking of importance; in every respect we must move in a more sustainable direction.\n\nThe list contains the tasks only in broad strokes; you can get a more comprehensive, detailed picture of environmental impacts and possible solutions by reading their descriptions as well.\n\n|&K28&[a]-  -  -  -  -  -  -[-]|\n|&K36&[a]Reducing waste, overconsumption, and waste generation[-]|\n|&B32&[k]What to do:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- choose quality over quantity; don’t buy unnecessary things; don’t stockpile more food and items than you truly need;\n\n- introduce at least one no-purchase day every week;\n\n- seek products made with sustainable production, because you vote for their makers with your money;\n\n- acquire durable, long-lasting items; if they break, try to repair them or have them repaired; avoid non-repairable, single-use tools;\n\n- choose wood or metal tools instead of plastic, as these are more likely to be recyclable;\n\n- plan what you will buy before every purchase and consider whether you truly need the item or service;\n\n- don’t decide based on discounts and promotions but based on an item’s usefulness;\n\n- consider used goods (clothes, household items) as well and try to pick good-quality ones among them;\n\n- don’t buy rarely used items, tools, or instruments; rather borrow or rent them;\n\n- for purchased food, pay attention to expiration dates; use what expires sooner first; freeze leftovers; learn home preservation techniques;\n\n- don’t prepare more food than will be eaten; if there is still leftover, think about what you could have done to avoid waste;\n\n- donate or sell your unnecessary but still working, usable items;\n\n- avoid single-use packaging (which becomes municipal waste due to non-recyclable material or contamination during use);\n\n- live with as little (all kinds of) packaging as possible (there is too much even of recyclable); seek returnable, recyclable, and reusable solutions; sort your waste selectively; compost what you can.[-]|\n|&B32&[k]Benefits:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- less production of new products (and packaging)—thus fewer greenhouse gases generated;\n\n- less waste and garbage produced;\n\n- less raw material and energy use;\n\n- reduced demand for arable land due to less food waste;\n\n- less pollution, fewer landfills, less waste incineration;\n\n- cleaner environment;\n\n- more mindful shoppers in stores;\n\n- supporting a circular economy that promotes repair, reuse, and recycling.[-]|\n\n|&K36&[a]Reducing meat consumption[-]|\n|&B32&[k]What to do:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- consume less red meat, processed meats, and meat-containing processed foods;\n\n- consume more plant proteins (e.g., legumes, mushrooms), products made from whole grains, and local, seasonal vegetables and fruits;\n\n- introduce meat-free days every week;\n\n- if you cannot give up meat, choose quality white meat from free-range, local sustainable farms.[-]|\n|&B32&[k]Benefits:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- less need for pasture and arable land; lower fertilizer and pesticide use;\n\n- fewer human-caused, intentional forest fires and less deforestation;\n\n- less use of drinking water;\n\n- reduced risk of infections and epidemics due to less meat processing;\n\n- fewer preservatives and other additives consumed;\n\n- better health and a more balanced life thanks to a mainly plant-based, dietary regimen;\n\n- less transport and packaging.[-]|\n\n|&K36&[a]Striving for self-sufficiency[-]|\n|&B32&[k]What to do:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- produce your staple foods yourself (vegetables, fruits, herbs, possibly poultry—eggs, white meat);\n\n- choose products from local farms and organic farms.[-]|\n|&B32&[k]Benefits:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- less dependence on supermarkets, industrial farms, and prices;\n\n- consumption of healthy foods;\n\n- gentler, more sustainable use of arable land and more efficient water use;\n\n- less transport and packaging;\n\n- fewer foods coming from afar, meaning less pressure and less deforestation and forest burning in tropical regions;\n\n- strengthening local farms and organic farms; growth in the number of new jobs;\n\n- prioritizing seasonal foods; eating freshly picked, ripe seasonal produce;\n\n- less food wasted;\n\n- better use of soil around houses and plots with gardens;\n\n- inspiring others in an exemplary way to pursue self-sufficiency;\n\n- producing your own foods, learning preservation techniques;\n\n- sharing best practices among each other; strengthening community.[-]|\n\n|&K36&[a]Reducing water use, protecting clean drinking water[-]|\n|&B32&[k]What to do:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- avoid using hazardous chemicals; use eco-friendly chemicals (paints, cosmetics, personal care, cleaning, washing);\n\n- store and use rainwater and greywater (water used once that is not drinkable but can still be used for irrigation);\n\n- use only as much tap drinking water as you absolutely need, because it takes a lot of energy and work to have potable water at the tap;\n\n- implement modern, efficient irrigation techniques (e.g.,  drip irrigation);\n\n- apply flow-reducing, water-saving techniques in the household (e.g., in the kitchen, bathroom, and toilet);\n\n- run your water-using household appliances (e.g., , dishwasher, washing machine) with full loads; that way they are more efficient with water and energy;\n\n- use a dishwasher instead of washing dishes under running water; when full it uses water more efficiently;\n\n- consume fewer water-intensive foods (e.g., , beef, pork, coffee, chocolate, rice, avocado);\n\n- instead of buying new clothes, get good-quality used garments (the fashion industry is extremely water-intensive and produces a lot of wastewater and greenhouse gases);\n\n- for new clothing, seek those made from organic cotton (and other eco-friendly materials—e.g., hemp, linen, organic cotton); producing the raw material and making the clothes burdens the environment less;\n\n- take antibiotics, antidepressants, sleeping pills, antihistamines, and other medicines only when absolutely necessary (their environmentally dangerous active substances often pass through wastewater treatment filters and enter natural waters);\n\n- never pour leftover or expired medicines, chemicals, or used oil down the drain; hand them in at a collection point;\n\n- plant lower-water-demand, climate-adapted species in your garden.[-]|\n|&B32&[k]Benefits:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- less wastewater produced;\n\n- more preserved, priceless drinking water;\n\n- cleaner lakes, rivers, and seas;\n\n- healthier natural ecosystems; a cleaner human environment.[-]|\n\n|&K36&[a]Reducing and transforming passenger and freight transport[-]|\n|&B32&[k]What to do:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- reduce kilometers traveled by motorized vehicles; prioritize healthy walking or cycling;\n\n- use energy-efficient electric vehicles and take public transport;\n\n- for in-store purchases and online orders, consider the necessity of products, their place of manufacture, and transport distance;\n\n- strive to meet all needs (food, goods, experiences) locally or domestically with services and products made as nearby as possible;\n\n- before long-distance travel, weigh its necessity, pros, and cons, and choose the most energy-efficient and least polluting mode of transport;\n\n- replace in-person meetings that require long trips with the virtual presence of videoconferences.[-]|\n|&B32&[k]Benefits:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- less energy (fuel) use;\n\n- less air pollution and greenhouse gas generation;\n\n- fewer people suffering from respiratory diseases;\n\n- less traffic on roads, waterways, and in the airspace;\n\n- less noise and light pollution.[-]|\n\n|&K36&[a]Curbing energy consumption[-]|\n|&B32&[k]What to do:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- travel less, combine trips, use energy-saving vehicles, and take public transport;\n\n- modernize your home heating to be more energy-efficient (e.g., heat pump heating); insulate your house and examine the causes of escaping or poorly utilized heat; don’t overheat rooms; aim for optimal temperatures;\n\n- try to generate the electricity you use yourself (e.g., using solar panels), or buy electricity from a provider that produces renewable energy;\n\n- use energy-intensive building cooling (air conditioning) only when justified and in moderation;\n\n- instead of building a new house, consider buying a well-built used one; this not only requires fewer raw materials, money, and energy, but also helps curb urban sprawl;\n\n- don’t oversize your home; determine its size based on the number of occupants;\n\n- before buying any new electrical device or appliance, consider whether you truly need it; disconnect existing ones when not needed;\n\n- consume less cooking oil; choose local oils instead of products coming from afar; switch to cooking methods and kitchen tools that require less oil and fat;\n\n- consume fewer carbohydrates (reduce sugar intake); choose foods with fewer calories and higher nutritional value;\n\n- generate less waste and garbage; avoid overpackaged goods (producing packaging is energy-intensive and expensive—for consumers too).[-]|\n|&B32&[k]Benefits:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- less dependence on grid energy;\n\n- lower use of fossil energy (oil, natural gas, coal);\n\n- reduced demand for arable land due to fewer energy crops grown;\n\n- less air, soil, and water pollution;\n\n- better health due to less oil and sugar consumption;\n\n- supporting a faster transition to renewable energy sources;\n\n- lower load on power plants; fewer greenhouse gases (coal plants) and hazardous substances (nuclear plants) produced.[-]|\n\n|&K36&[a]Environmental activities[-]|\n|&B32&[k]What to do:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- support the work of environmental organizations, as their work contributes to building a more sustainable future;\n\n- take part in volunteer environmental protection actions; sign environmental petitions;\n\n- report environmental damage to the competent authorities;\n\n- care for the natural world and all living beings in it;\n\n- do everything you can to avoid polluting the air, the soil, and the water;\n\n- green your surroundings; plant trees; create shelters, water sources, and a garden pond for animals in your garden;\n\n- if you must travel a lot or carry out transport activities, offset your greenhouse gas emissions: pay into services that support emission-reduction projects (e.g., reforestation, building solar parks);\n\n- do not choose food or items made from endangered species;\n\n- do not buy cosmetics developed with animal testing and do not use treatments that use parts of animals;\n\n- speak up about the importance of environmental protection, climate protection, and sustainability on your social channels and share how you yourself contribute to building a more sustainable future.[-]|\n|&B32&[k]Benefits:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- a cleaner human and natural environment;\n\n- a strengthened animal and plant world; better protection of biodiversity;\n\n- a healthier natural world, which also contributes to human well-being.[-]|\n\n|&K36&[a]Developing humanity (compassion)[-]|\n|&B32&[k]What to do:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- support those in need; help people in trouble (financial support; donating surplus household items and leftover food);\n\n- care about others; behave with more understanding toward others;\n\n- strive to resolve your conflicts peacefully and encourage others to do the same.[-]|\n|&B32&[k]Benefits:[-]|\n|&B28&[s]- people who care for each other live in more balanced, happier societies;\n\n- less hunger and a rising standard of living lead to less aggression, fewer social tensions, and fewer causes of war;\n\n- humanity (compassion) also positively affects climate change mitigation, because by listening to each other and building trust, the advice for a more sustainable lifestyle reaches more people, more understand the necessity, and more take action.[-]|\n\n|&K36&[a]Having one fewer child[-]|\n\nThis point comes last, but in reality it would belong at the top, because although very personal, [z]it is a more effective decision than any other climate action.[-]\nWhy?\nBecause for every single person it is true that throughout their life—from beginning to end—due to needs and wants, they place varying burdens on Earth and, depending on their activities, continuously contribute more or less to the intensification of environmental impacts.\n\nEarth is becoming overpopulated (every year we are more than 80 million more), and in parallel our comfort, mobility, and entertainment needs are constantly growing; [p]as a result, humanity increasingly overloads Earth.[-]\n\nAccording to experts dealing with demography and population growth, a peak will come after which the human population will be forced to decline due to climate change and the critical reduction of natural resources.\n\nThe demographic explosion is thus pushing the world toward an ecological tipping point, which we should by no means reach because it would have unpredictable consequences—therefore, besides making our lives more sustainable, we should also slow (or better yet reduce) population growth.\n\n|&K36&[k]What should you do to make your life more sustainable?[-]|\n|&K36&[z]Live your life while thinking of the next generations and all living beings on Earth—they, too, need and will need a clean environment in the future: clean air, clean water, and clean, productive soil.[-]|\n
